def __init__(self, params=None, auto_init=True):

"""Create a FileDownloader object with the given options.

@param auto_init Whether to load the default extractors and print header (if verbose).

Set to 'no_verbose_header' to not print the header

"""

if params is None:

params = {}

self.params = params

self._ies = {}

self._ies_instances = {}

self._pps = {k: [] for k in POSTPROCESS_WHEN}

self._printed_messages = set()

self._first_webpage_request = True

self._post_hooks = []

self._close_hooks = []

self._progress_hooks = []

self._postprocessor_hooks = []

self._download_retcode = 0

self._num_downloads = 0

self._num_videos = 0

self._playlist_level = 0

self._playlist_urls = set()

self.cache = Cache(self)

self.__header_cookies = []

# compat for API: load plugins if they have not already

if not all_plugins_loaded.value:

load_all_plugins()

stdout = sys.stderr if self.params.get('logtostderr') else sys.stdout

self._out_files = Namespace(

out=stdout,

error=sys.stderr,

screen=sys.stderr if self.params.get('quiet') else stdout,

)

try:

windows_enable_vt_mode()

except Exception as e:

self.write_debug(f'Failed to enable VT mode: {e}')

# hehe "immutable" namespace

self._out_files.console = next(filter(supports_terminal_sequences, (sys.stderr, sys.stdout)), None)

if self.params.get('no_color'):

if self.params.get('color') is not None:

self.params.setdefault('_warnings', []).append(

'Overwriting params from "color" with "no_color"')

self.params['color'] = 'no_color'

term_allow_color = os.getenv('TERM', '').lower() != 'dumb'

base_no_color = bool(os.getenv('NO_COLOR'))

def process_color_policy(stream):

stream_name = {sys.stdout: 'stdout', sys.stderr: 'stderr'}[stream]

policy = traverse_obj(self.params, ('color', (stream_name, None), {str}, any)) or 'auto'

if policy in ('auto', 'auto-tty', 'no_color-tty'):

no_color = base_no_color

if policy.endswith('tty'):

no_color = policy.startswith('no_color')

if term_allow_color and supports_terminal_sequences(stream):

return 'no_color' if no_color else True

return False

assert policy in ('always', 'never', 'no_color'), policy

return {'always': True, 'never': False}.get(policy, policy)

self._allow_colors = Namespace(**{

name: process_color_policy(stream)

for name, stream in self._out_files.items_ if name != 'console'

})

system_deprecation = _get_system_deprecation()

if system_deprecation:

self.deprecated_feature(system_deprecation.replace('\n', '\n '))

elif self.params.get('warn_when_outdated'):

if outdated_warning := _get_outdated_warning():

self.report_warning(outdated_warning)

if self.params.get('allow_unplayable_formats'):

self.report_warning(

f'You have asked for {self._format_err("UNPLAYABLE", self.Styles.EMPHASIS)} formats to be listed/downloaded. '

'This is a developer option intended for debugging. \n'

' If you experience any issues while using this option, '

f'{self._format_err("DO NOT", self.Styles.ERROR)} open a bug report')

if self.params.get('bidi_workaround', False):

try:

import pty

master, slave = pty.openpty()

width = shutil.get_terminal_size().columns

width_args = [] if width is None else ['-w', str(width)]

sp_kwargs = {'stdin': subprocess.PIPE, 'stdout': slave, 'stderr': self._out_files.error}

try:

self._output_process = Popen(['bidiv', *width_args], **sp_kwargs)

except OSError:

self._output_process = Popen(['fribidi', '-c', 'UTF-8', *width_args], **sp_kwargs)

self._output_channel = os.fdopen(master, 'rb')

except OSError as ose:

if ose.errno == errno.ENOENT:

self.report_warning(

'Could not find fribidi executable, ignoring --bidi-workaround. '

'Make sure that fribidi is an executable file in one of the directories in your $PATH.')

else:

raise

# Note: this must be after plugins are loaded

self.params['js_runtimes'] = self.params.get('js_runtimes', {'deno': {}})

self._clean_js_runtimes(self.params['js_runtimes'])

self.params['remote_components'] = set(self.params.get('remote_components', ()))

self._clean_remote_components(self.params['remote_components'])

self.params['compat_opts'] = set(self.params.get('compat_opts', ()))

self.params['http_headers'] = HTTPHeaderDict(std_headers, self.params.get('http_headers'))

self._load_cookies(self.params['http_headers'].get('Cookie')) # compat

self.params['http_headers'].pop('Cookie', None)

if auto_init and auto_init != 'no_verbose_header':

self.print_debug_header()

def check_deprecated(param, option, suggestion):

if self.params.get(param) is not None:

self.report_warning(f'{option} is deprecated. Use {suggestion} instead')

return True

return False

check_deprecated('useid', '--id', '-o "%(id)s.%(ext)s"')

for msg in self.params.get('_warnings', []):

self.report_warning(msg)

for msg in self.params.get('_deprecation_warnings', []):

self.deprecated_feature(msg)

if impersonate_target := self.params.get('impersonate'):

if not self._impersonate_target_available(impersonate_target):

raise YoutubeDLError(

f'Impersonate target "{impersonate_target}" is not available. '

f'Use --list-impersonate-targets to see available targets. '

f'You may be missing dependencies required to support this target.')

if 'list-formats' in self.params['compat_opts']:

self.params['listformats_table'] = False

if 'overwrites' not in self.params and self.params.get('nooverwrites') is not None:

# nooverwrites was unnecessarily changed to overwrites

# in 0c3d0f51778b153f65c21906031c2e091fcfb641

# This ensures compatibility with both keys

self.params['overwrites'] = not self.params['nooverwrites']

elif self.params.get('overwrites') is None:

self.params.pop('overwrites', None)

else:

self.params['nooverwrites'] = not self.params['overwrites']

if self.params.get('simulate') is None and any((

self.params.get('list_thumbnails'),

self.params.get('listformats'),

self.params.get('listsubtitles'),

)):

self.params['simulate'] = 'list_only'

self.params.setdefault('forceprint', {})

self.params.setdefault('print_to_file', {})

# Compatibility with older syntax

if not isinstance(params['forceprint'], dict):

self.params['forceprint'] = {'video': params['forceprint']}

if auto_init:

self.add_default_info_extractors()

if (sys.platform != 'win32'

and sys.getfilesystemencoding() in ['ascii', 'ANSI_X3.4-1968']

and not self.params.get('restrictfilenames', False)):

# Unicode filesystem API will throw errors (#1474, #13027)

self.report_warning(

'Assuming --restrict-filenames since file system encoding '

'cannot encode all characters. '

'Set the LC_ALL environment variable to fix this.')

self.params['restrictfilenames'] = True

self._parse_outtmpl()

# Creating format selector here allows us to catch syntax errors before the extraction

self.format_selector = (

self.params.get('format') if self.params.get('format') in (None, '-')

else self.params['format'] if callable(self.params['format'])

else self.build_format_selector(self.params['format']))

hooks = {

'post_hooks': self.add_post_hook,

'progress_hooks': self.add_progress_hook,

'postprocessor_hooks': self.add_postprocessor_hook,

}

for opt, fn in hooks.items():

for ph in self.params.get(opt, []):

fn(ph)

for pp_def_raw in self.params.get('postprocessors', []):

pp_def = dict(pp_def_raw)

when = pp_def.pop('when', 'post_process')

self.add_post_processor(

get_postprocessor(pp_def.pop('key'))(self, **pp_def),

when=when)

def preload_download_archive(fn):

"""Preload the archive, if any is specified"""

archive = set()

if fn is None:

return archive

elif not is_path_like(fn):

return fn

self.write_debug(f'Loading archive file {fn!r}')

try:

with locked_file(fn, 'r', encoding='utf-8') as archive_file:

for line in archive_file:

archive.add(line.strip())

except OSError as ioe:

if ioe.errno != errno.ENOENT:

raise

return archive

self.archive = preload_download_archive(self.params.get('download_archive'))

def _clean_js_runtimes(self, runtimes):

if not (

isinstance(runtimes, dict)

and all(isinstance(k, str) and (v is None or isinstance(v, dict)) for k, v in runtimes.items())

):

raise ValueError('Invalid js_runtimes format, expected a dict of {runtime: {config}}')

if unsupported_runtimes := runtimes.keys() - supported_js_runtimes.value.keys():

self.report_warning(

f'Ignoring unsupported JavaScript runtime(s): {", ".join(unsupported_runtimes)}.'

f' Supported runtimes: {", ".join(supported_js_runtimes.value.keys())}.')

for rt in unsupported_runtimes:

runtimes.pop(rt)

def _clean_remote_components(self, remote_components: set):

if unsupported_remote_components := set(remote_components) - set(supported_remote_components.value):

self.report_warning(

f'Ignoring unsupported remote component(s): {", ".join(unsupported_remote_components)}.'

f' Supported remote components: {", ".join(supported_remote_components.value)}.')

for rt in unsupported_remote_components:

remote_components.remove(rt)

@functools.cached_property

def _js_runtimes(self):

runtimes = {}

for name, config in self.params.get('js_runtimes', {}).items():

runtime_cls = supported_js_runtimes.value.get(name)

runtimes[name] = runtime_cls(path=config.get('path')) if runtime_cls else None

return runtimes

def warn_if_short_id(self, argv):

# short YouTube ID starting with dash?

idxs = [

i for i, a in enumerate(argv)

if re.match(r'^-[0-9A-Za-z_-]{10}$', a)]

if idxs:

correct_argv = (

['yt-dlp']

+ [a for i, a in enumerate(argv) if i not in idxs]

+ ['--'] + [argv[i] for i in idxs]

)

self.report_warning(

'Long argument string detected. '

f'Use -- to separate parameters and URLs, like this:\n{shell_quote(correct_argv)}')

def add_info_extractor(self, ie):

"""Add an InfoExtractor object to the end of the list."""

ie_key = ie.ie_key()

self._ies[ie_key] = ie

if not isinstance(ie, type):

self._ies_instances[ie_key] = ie

ie.set_downloader(self)

def get_info_extractor(self, ie_key):

"""

Get an instance of an IE with name ie_key, it will try to get one from

the _ies list, if there's no instance it will create a new one and add

it to the extractor list.

"""

ie = self._ies_instances.get(ie_key)

if ie is None:

ie = get_info_extractor(ie_key)()

self.add_info_extractor(ie)

return ie

def add_default_info_extractors(self):

"""

Add the InfoExtractors returned by gen_extractors to the end of the list

"""

all_ies = {ie.IE_NAME.lower(): ie for ie in gen_extractor_classes()}

all_ies['end'] = UnsupportedURLIE()

try:

ie_names = orderedSet_from_options(

self.params.get('allowed_extractors', ['default']), {

'all': list(all_ies),

'default': [name for name, ie in all_ies.items() if ie._ENABLED],

}, use_regex=True)

except re.error as e:

raise ValueError(f'Wrong regex for allowed_extractors: {e.pattern}')

for name in ie_names:

self.add_info_extractor(all_ies[name])

self.write_debug(f'Loaded {len(ie_names)} extractors')

def add_post_processor(self, pp, when='post_process'):

"""Add a PostProcessor object to the end of the chain."""

assert when in POSTPROCESS_WHEN, f'Invalid when={when}'

self._pps[when].append(pp)

pp.set_downloader(self)

def add_post_hook(self, ph):

"""Add the post hook"""

self._post_hooks.append(ph)

def add_close_hook(self, ch):

"""Add a close hook, called when YoutubeDL.close() is called"""

assert callable(ch), 'Close hook must be callable'

self._close_hooks.append(ch)

def add_progress_hook(self, ph):

"""Add the download progress hook"""

self._progress_hooks.append(ph)

def add_postprocessor_hook(self, ph):

"""Add the postprocessing progress hook"""

self._postprocessor_hooks.append(ph)

for pps in self._pps.values():

for pp in pps:

pp.add_progress_hook(ph)

def _bidi_workaround(self, message):

if not hasattr(self, '_output_channel'):

return message

assert hasattr(self, '_output_process')

assert isinstance(message, str)

line_count = message.count('\n') + 1

self._output_process.stdin.write((message + '\n').encode())

self._output_process.stdin.flush()

res = ''.join(self._output_channel.readline().decode()

for _ in range(line_count))

return res[:-len('\n')]

def _write_string(self, message, out=None, only_once=False):

if only_once:

if message in self._printed_messages:

return

self._printed_messages.add(message)

write_string(message, out=out, encoding=self.params.get('encoding'))

def to_stdout(self, message, skip_eol=False, quiet=None):

"""Print message to stdout"""

if quiet is not None:

self.deprecation_warning('"YoutubeDL.to_stdout" no longer accepts the argument quiet. '

'Use "YoutubeDL.to_screen" instead')

if skip_eol is not False:

self.deprecation_warning('"YoutubeDL.to_stdout" no longer accepts the argument skip_eol. '

'Use "YoutubeDL.to_screen" instead')

self._write_string(f'{self._bidi_workaround(message)}\n', self._out_files.out)

def to_screen(self, message, skip_eol=False, quiet=None, only_once=False):

"""Print message to screen if not in quiet mode"""

if self.params.get('logger'):

self.params['logger'].debug(message)

return

if (self.params.get('quiet') if quiet is None else quiet) and not self.params.get('verbose'):

return

self._write_string(

'{}{}'.format(self._bidi_workaround(message), ('' if skip_eol else '\n')),

# Maintainers

This file lists the maintainers of yt-dlp and their major contributions. See the [Changelog](/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/blob/master/Changelog.md) for more details.

You can also find lists of all [contributors of yt-dlp](/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTORS) and [authors of youtube-dl](https://github.com/ytdl-org/youtube-dl/blob/master/AUTHORS)

## Core Maintainers

Core Maintainers are responsible for reviewing and merging contributions, publishing releases, and steering the overall direction of the project.

**You can contact the core maintainers via`maintainers@yt-dlp.org`.** This email address is **NOT** a support channel. [Open an issue](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/new/choose) if you need help or want to report a bug.

### [coletdjnz](https://github.com/coletdjnz)

[](https://github.com/sponsors/coletdjnz)

  * Overhauled the networking stack and implemented support for `requests` and `curl_cffi` (`--impersonate`) HTTP clients
  * Reworked the plugin architecture to support installing plugins across all yt-dlp distributions (exe, pip, etc.)
  * Implemented support for external JavaScript runtimes/engines
  * Maintains support for YouTube
  * Added and fixed support for various other sites



### [bashonly](https://github.com/bashonly)

  * Rewrote and maintains the build/release workflows and the self-updater: executables, automated/nightly/master releases, `--update-to`
  * Overhauled external downloader cookie handling
  * Helped in implementing support for external JavaScript runtimes/engines
  * Added `--cookies-from-browser` support for Firefox containers
  * Maintains support for sites like YouTube, Vimeo, Twitter, TikTok, etc
  * Added support for various sites



### [Grub4K](https://github.com/Grub4K)

[](https://github.com/sponsors/Grub4K) [](https://ko-fi.com/Grub4K)

  * `--update-to`, self-updater rewrite, automated/nightly/master releases
  * Reworked internals like `traverse_obj`, various core refactors and bugs fixes
  * Implemented proper progress reporting for parallel downloads
  * Implemented support for external JavaScript runtimes/engines
  * Improved/fixed/added Bundestag, crunchyroll, pr0gramm, Twitter, WrestleUniverse etc



## Inactive Core Maintainers

### [pukkandan](https://github.com/pukkandan)

[](https://ko-fi.com/pukkandan) [](https://github.com/sponsors/pukkandan)

  * Founder of the fork
  * Lead Maintainer from 2021-2024



### [shirt](https://github.com/shirt-dev)

[](https://ko-fi.com/shirt)

  * Multithreading (`-N`) and aria2c support for fragment downloads
  * Support for media initialization and discontinuity in HLS
  * The self-updater (`-U`)



### [Ashish0804](https://github.com/Ashish0804)

[](https://ko-fi.com/ashish0804)

  * Added support for new websites BiliIntl, DiscoveryPlusIndia, OlympicsReplay, PlanetMarathi, ShemarooMe, Utreon, Zee5 etc
  * Added playlist/series downloads for Hotstar, ParamountPlus, Rumble, SonyLIV, Trovo, TubiTv, Voot etc
  * Improved/fixed support for HiDive, HotStar, Hungama, LBRY, LinkedInLearning, Mxplayer, SonyLiv, TV2, Vimeo, VLive etc



### [sepro](https://github.com/seproDev)

  * UX improvements: Warn when ffmpeg is missing, warn when double-clicking exe
  * Helped in implementing support for external JavaScript runtimes/engines
  * Code cleanup: Remove dead extractors, mark extractors as broken, enable/apply ruff rules
  * Improved/fixed/added ArdMediathek, DRTV, Floatplane, MagentaMusik, Naver, Nebula, OnDemandKorea, Vbox7 etc



## Triage Maintainers

Triage Maintainers are frequent contributors who can manage issues and pull requests.

  * [gamer191](https://github.com/gamer191)
  * [garret1317](https://github.com/garret1317)
  * [pzhlkj6612](https://github.com/pzhlkj6612)
  * [DTrombett](https://github.com/dtrombett)
  * [doe1080](https://github.com/doe1080)
  * [grqz](https://github.com/grqz)

### Checklist

  * I've checked that all URLs and arguments with special characters are [properly quoted or escaped](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/wiki/FAQ#video-url-contains-an-ampersand--and-im-getting-some-strange-output-1-2839-or-v-is-not-recognized-as-an-internal-or-external-command)
  * I've searched [known issues](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/3766), [the FAQ](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/wiki/FAQ), and the [bugtracker](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues?q=is%3Aissue%20-label%3Aspam%20%20) for similar issues **including closed ones**. DO NOT post duplicates

### EDIT: This is fixed in the latest release. Update!

* * *

Executable users:
    
    
    yt-dlp -U
    

Users who installed with pip/etc should make sure to include the `[default]` extra when upgrading, e.g.:
    
    
    pip install -U "yt-dlp[default]"
    

The `yt-dlp-ejs` package is already included in the Github release executables and the `default` extra from PyPI. If you have installed yt-dlp **some other way** , then you may need to add this to your command the first time you run the new version:
    
    
    --remote-components ejs:github
    

And so that you actually benefit from the fix, make sure you have a [supported JavaScript runtime installed](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/wiki/EJS)

* * *

old/original message

    --extractor-args "yout…

## Intractable issues

  * **[[YouTube] This content isn't available, try again later. #11426](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/11426)**
    * You are exceeding the rate limit. Refer to [the wiki on how to avoid](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/wiki/Extractors#this-content-isnt-available-try-again-later).
  * **[Passing Youtube cookies doesn't seem to work; cookies are being invalidated quickly #8227](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/8227)**
    * [How to effectively export YouTube cookies](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/wiki/Extractors#exporting-youtube-cookies)
  * **[[youtube] Sign in to confirm you’re not a bot #10128](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/10128)**
    * Your IP has been blocked by YouTube while you are logged out. You can [pass logged-in cookies](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/wiki/Extractors#exporting-youtube-cookies); however, doing so may get your account blocked. The safer solution is to use a different IP.
    * To prevent this, [try using a PO Token provider](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/wiki/PO-Token-Guide), though it will not help if your IP is already blocked.
  * **[[youtube] "Video unavailable" with cookies - YouTube blocking accounts from web #10085](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/10085)**
    * Your account has been blocked by YouTube, or the video is not available in your region.
    * Avoid passing cookies, or add a [sleep delay](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp#workarounds) to each download.
  * **[[Youtube] Immediate HTTP Error 403 on download #11868](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/11868)**
    * Try using `--force-ipv4`, try using yt-dlp from a different IP address (e.g. disable your VPN), try using logged-in cookies if you were using yt-dlp logged-out, or try using yt-dlp without cookies if you were using logged-in cookies

# External issues

  * [ffmpeg can't seek in Youtube's iOS m3u8 streams / `--download-sections` only downloads audio #9552](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/9552)
    * Use `-S proto:https` or `--extractor-args "youtube:player_client=default,-ios"`
  * [`--cookies-from-browser` "Permission denied" errors when Chrome/chromium-based browser is open in Windows #7271](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/7271)
    * Try after closing chrome completely OR
    * Launch chrome from command line w/ `chrome.exe --disable-features=LockProfileCookieDatabase`
    * Alternatively, you can [install](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp#installing-plugins) the [ChomeCookieUnlock yt-dlp plugin](https://github.com/seproDev/yt-dlp-ChromeCookieUnlock)
  * [`--cookies-from-browser`: WARNING: failed to decrypt with DPAPI / ERROR: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'decode' #10927](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/10927)
  * [[youtube] Is downloading a livestream in 1440p or 2160p no longer available? #11262](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/11262)
  * [[Youtube] 8k VR180 SBS videos no longer available #9903](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/9903)
    * Use `--extractor-arg "youtube:player_client=android_vr,default"`
  * [[Youtube] throttling and inconsistent speed in Russia #10443](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/10443)
    * [Workarounds](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/10443#issuecomment-2248940967)
  * [[Discord bot] Music stops in the middle #8854](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/8854)
  * [[youtube] Endless "Incomplete data received" when downloading playlist #10394](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/10394)
    * Don't use `--extractor-retries infinite`
  * [FFMPEG "Invalid data found when processing input" on live/post-live/dash videos (duplicate ftyp) #8641](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/8641)
    * Regression in ffmpeg 6.1. Upgrade to ffmpeg 6.1.1 or to [master build](https://github.com/yt-dlp/FFmpeg-Builds/releases) revision `N-112916` or later
  * [[youtube] "Invalid data found when processing input" / ffmpeg errors on HDR VP9 in mp4 #7541](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/7541)
    * ffmpeg bug. Upgrade to ffmpeg 7.0.1 or to the latest [master build](https://github.com/yt-dlp/FFmpeg-Builds/releases)
  * [`--mark-watched` fails with urlopen error #8149](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/8149)
    * Disable pi-hole or whitelist `s.youtube.com`
  * [Chapter Embedding Results in Unnamed Chapters When Using Recent FFmpeg Builds #6859](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/6859)
    * ffmpeg regression. Use <https://github.com/yt-dlp/FFmpeg-Builds> or upgrade to 6.1.1 or newer
  * [yt-dlp is detected as a virus #25](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/25)
    * It's a false positive. Complain to your vendor. There is nothing we can do
  * [Incomplete Data Recieved #1787](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/1787)
    * Broken from Youtube's side. If downloading comments, use `-i` to ignore the error
  * [Wrong year in metadata in M4A, MP4, FLAC format #3087](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/3087)
    * Workaround: `--parse-metadata "%(release_year,upload_date).4s:(?P<meta_date>.+)"`
  * [pyinstaller temp files are not cleaned up when using yt-dlp.exe with mpv #10294](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/10294)
  * [Long Start-Up Time for `yt-dlp_macos` #10425](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/10425)
  * [`--download-sections` / ffmpeg fails to seek in a 26+ hour long Twitch m3u8 #5372](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/5372)
  * [Using proxy and `--download-sections`/ ffmpeg fails with HTTP Error 400/401/403 #12915](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/12915)



# FAQ

See <https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/wiki/FAQ>

  * **[How to avoid Youtube's new "Super Resolution" AI-upscaled formats #15325](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/15325)**
  * **[Getting deno to work in Termux. #15095 (comment)](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/15095#issuecomment-3544324838)**
    * Run a full Termux upgrade with `pkg update && pkg upgrade` before `pkg install deno`
  * **[[YouTube] Enhanced bitrate no longer available to download? #14133 (comment)](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/14133#issuecomment-3217679575)**
  * [**Filename too long**](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/1136#issuecomment-932077195)
    * Use `-o "%(title).150B [%(id)s].%(ext)s"`
  * **[[YouTube]`--write-comments`: "Incomplete data received. Giving up after 3 retries" warnings #15435](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/15435)**
  * **[twitter: No video could be found in this tweet #14742](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/14742)**
  * [[Question] odd ba* format selection? #979 (comment)](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/979#issuecomment-919629354)
    * Generally do not use `ba*`
  * [Fix playlist_index's inconsistent behavior #302](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/pull/302)
    * Check `playlist_autonumber` and `--compat-option playlist-index`
  * [yt-dlp python module not compiling with pyinstaller #3845](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/3845)
    * Use `bundle/pyinstaller.py`
  * [Subtitle file is not deleted after being embedded #630 (comment)](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/630#issuecomment-893659460)
    * Use `--compat-option no-keep-subs`
  * [`--download-sections`/`--sponsorblock-remove` does not cut at exact point #4216](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/4216) / [YouTube Clip Downloads have unintented extra beginning part with no video #5080](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/5080)
    * Use `--force-keyframes-at-cuts`
  * [Duplicating pull request from youtube-dl to yt-dlp #4202](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/4202)
  * [How to check in browser if the video is DRM protected](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/4062#issuecomment-1153474056)
  * [\--cookies-from-browser for a chrome/firefox like browser or non-default install location #2903](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/2903)
  * [What are yt-dlp's error codes? #4262 (comment)](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/4262#issuecomment-1173133105)
  * [Extractor option `language` for `crunchyrollbeta` #4640](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/4640)
  * [Ability to strip Emoji from downloaded file  #4836](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/4836) / [File names use "full-width" special characters: '？' vs '?' #5014](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/5014)
  * [[Youtube] Extract exact timestamps #1803](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/1803)
  * [[Feature Request] Crop to square thumbnail when embedding in MP3s #429 (comment)](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/429#issuecomment-2282554440)
  * Download only videos with subtitles 
    * `--parse-metadata "%(subtitles.\:.0.ext|)s:^(?!\[\])(?P<has_subs>.)" -v --match-filter has_subs`
  * [How do I rename previously-downloaded files with nothing but the youtube video ID? #5692](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/5692)
  * Remove specific fields from info-json - [[Suggestion] Redact `formats` in info json with an option #455 (comment)](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/455#issuecomment-1367741786)
  * About subtitles in mp4 container - [Convert webvtt subtitles in mp4 into useable format #5833 (comment)](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/5833#issuecomment-1358246240)
  * [Find the API option for a CLI argument #5859 (comment)](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/5859#issuecomment-1363938900)
    * Use <https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/blob/master/devscripts/cli_to_api.py>
  * [[YouTube] `youtube:skip=translated_subs` doesn't work for some videos. #3875](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/3875)
  * [Youtube bestvideo and vp9 preference. #1232 (comment)](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/1232#issuecomment-939635345)
  * [repo: git log broken by SSH signature #7322](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/7322)
  * [download comments into separate comments.json file #2372 (comment)](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/2372#issuecomment-1506413976)
  * [How to force a conversion to a specific video codec? #7607 (comment)](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/7607#issuecomment-1636960750)
  * [How to download youtube videos in mp4 format? #8880](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/8880)
  * [How do I properly pass my Soundcloud oauth token to yt-dlp? #12249 (comment)](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/12249#issuecomment-2628937389)
  * [[youtube] 256kbps music formats not being extracted #12455 (comment)](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/12455#issuecomment-2677077342)
  * [[PYI-12704:ERROR] Failed to extract Cryptodome\Cipher_ARC4.pyd: decompression resulted in return code -1! #16522](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/16522)
    * You probably don't have enough free disk space on the drive where your temp dir is located

## Description

[](https://github.com/Lithira-Amarasinghe)

[Lithira-Amarasinghe](https://github.com/Lithira-Amarasinghe)

opened [on May 2, 2026](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/16615#issue-4368752469)

Issue body actions

### Checklist

  * I'm requesting a feature unrelated to a specific site
  * I've looked through the [README](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp#readme)
  * I've verified that I have **updated yt-dlp to nightly or master** ([update instructions](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp#update-channels))
  * I've searched the [bugtracker](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues?q=is%3Aissue%20-label%3Aspam%20%20) for similar requests **including closed ones**. DO NOT post duplicates
  * I've read the [policy against AI/LLM contributions](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#automated-contributions-ai--llm-policy) and understand I may be blocked from the repository if it is violated



### Provide a description that is worded well enough to be understood

The main issue identified is format IDs are not standardized so when there are multiple Periods in a DASH-manifest it's difficult to decide the Period to which a specific Format is related. Following list is the Format IDs mentioned in the verbose output.

images_1-0,images_1-1, a0-0, a0-1, v2-0,v8, v1-0, v7, v4, v1-1, v0, v6-0, v3-0, v5-0

Based on the above Format ID list, we can see that some ids have structures like "a0-0" but some others have "v8" like structure. So it's confusing that which is the relevant Period of specific Format. As a result of that there is an ambiguity in selecting the audio and muted-video when a user need to download a specific Period.

This unidentifiability cause to download a wired video which means when user needed to download a specific Period, they may combine Formats that seems like related to that period but final output may be a combination of Formats in different Periods.

To ensure consistency and clarity, Format IDs should be standardized across the system. A structured format such as a0-0 or v2-0 is recommended, where the number following the hyphen indicates the corresponding Period ID. This approach makes Format IDs easier to read, manage, and trace back to their related periods

### Provide verbose output that clearly demonstrates the problem

  * Run **your** yt-dlp command with **-vU** flag added (`yt-dlp -vU <your command line>`)
  * If using API, add `'verbose': True` to `YoutubeDL` params instead
  * Copy the WHOLE output (starting with `[debug] Command-line config`) and insert it below

Issue body actions

### Checklist

  * I'm reporting a new site support request
  * I've verified that I have **updated yt-dlp to nightly or master** ([update instructions](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp#update-channels))
  * I've checked that all provided URLs are playable in a browser with the same IP and same login details
  * I've checked that none of provided URLs [violate any copyrights](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#is-the-website-primarily-used-for-piracy) or contain any [DRM](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Digital_rights_management) to the best of my knowledge
  * I've searched the [bugtracker](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues?q=is%3Aissue%20-label%3Aspam%20%20) for similar requests **including closed ones**. DO NOT post duplicates
  * I've read the [policy against AI/LLM contributions](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#automated-contributions-ai--llm-policy) and understand I may be blocked from the repository if it is violated
  * I've read about [sharing account credentials](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#are-you-willing-to-share-account-details-if-needed) and am willing to share it if required



### Region

United States of America

### Example URLs

<https://fox4kc.com/video/fbi-probe-into-kansas-city-mayor-pro-tem-expands-new-line-of-inquiry-revealed/11665956/>

### Provide a description that is worded well enough to be understood

I am able to play this video in Firefox. I have yt-dlp configured to use cookies from Firefox. It downloads videos from other sites but it says videos from this site cannot be downloaded because the site returns http error 403.

### Provide verbose output that clearly demonstrates the problem

  * Run **your** yt-dlp command with **-vU** flag added (`yt-dlp -vU <your command line>`)
  * If using API, add `'verbose': True` to `YoutubeDL` params instead
  * Copy the WHOLE output (starting with `[debug] Command-line config`) and insert it below

## Description

[](https://github.com/mayconhvab)

[mayconhvab](https://github.com/mayconhvab)

opened [on Apr 30, 2026](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/16601#issue-4359093522)

Issue body actions

### Checklist

  * I'm reporting that yt-dlp is broken on a **supported** site
  * I've verified that I have **updated yt-dlp to nightly or master** ([update instructions](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp#update-channels))
  * I've checked that all provided URLs are playable in a browser with the same IP and same login details
  * I've checked that all URLs and arguments with special characters are [properly quoted or escaped](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/wiki/FAQ#video-url-contains-an-ampersand--and-im-getting-some-strange-output-1-2839-or-v-is-not-recognized-as-an-internal-or-external-command)
  * I've searched [known issues](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/3766), [the FAQ](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/wiki/FAQ), and the [bugtracker](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues?q=is%3Aissue%20-label%3Aspam%20%20) for similar issues **including closed ones**. DO NOT post duplicates
  * I've read the [policy against AI/LLM contributions](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#automated-contributions-ai--llm-policy) and understand I may be blocked from the repository if it is violated
  * I've read about [sharing account credentials](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#are-you-willing-to-share-account-details-if-needed) and I'm willing to share it if required



### Region

Brazil

### Provide a description that is worded well enough to be understood

Hi, currently when using the latest version of yt-dlp on Termux, I noticed that when using '-F', the audio formats and some formats like VP9 and AV1 have simply disappeared.  
​It's also not showing 2K and 4K quality—I believe 8K doesn't show up either—and the M4A and Opus formats are not visible as well.  
​I'd like to know what's going on?  
​Or is this a bug that unfortunately hasn't been fixed yet?  
​For more context, here’s what I did: I cleared all cache and data from YouTube and my browser. I’m using the latest version of Google Chrome from the Play Store, updated through the official store without using any third-party software like APK Mirror.  
​After clearing the cache for both apps, I opened Google Chrome and searched for 'YouTube' in the search bar.  
​Then, I went to tools and filtered by 'last date' and 'last hour'.  
​After that, I searched for a very recent video because I believe that through Google Chrome's search sources, when I open YouTube, the software detects the most recent API and info from the YouTube server for the browser. This works for YouTube as a whole, and I believe it might improve the quality a bit.  
​But speaking of which, the formats cannot be accessed when using: yt-dlp <https://youtu.be/WqbJT_vC0rs>  
​When downloading, the video only downloads in MP4 1080p H264 AVC, and it doesn't download in the higher quality that exists.  
​I just opened the video and copied the link via the 'share' button, right there in the video info on YouTube.  
​Let me know if there's any information missing.  
​I apologize to the moderator who told me never to tag LLM again; I don't really understand that tool, but if this topic I created lets me post this info without tagging it, I'm being truly sincere in what I'm doing.  
​I don't know if it will allow the LLM tag or not.  
​But that's it.  
​YouTube is not letting me check formats with '-F' and I'm getting a 403 error.  
​Thank you very much in advance, dear friends."

### Provide verbose output that clearly demonstrates the problem

  * Run **your** yt-dlp command with **-vU** flag added (`yt-dlp -vU <your command line>`)
  * If using API, add `'verbose': True` to `YoutubeDL` params instead
  * Copy the WHOLE output (starting with `[debug] Command-line config`) and insert it below

# Support wreq as alternative to curl_cffi that works on FreeBSD #16577

## Description

[](https://github.com/dbohdan)

[dbohdan](https://github.com/dbohdan)

opened [on Apr 26, 2026](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/16577#issue-4330182519)

Issue body actions

### Checklist

  * I'm requesting a feature unrelated to a specific site
  * I've looked through the [README](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp#readme)
  * I've verified that I have **updated yt-dlp to nightly or master** ([update instructions](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp#update-channels))
  * I've searched the [bugtracker](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues?q=is%3Aissue%20-label%3Aspam%20%20) for similar requests **including closed ones**. DO NOT post duplicates
  * I've read the [policy against AI/LLM contributions](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#automated-contributions-ai--llm-policy) and understand I may be blocked from the repository if it is violated



### Provide a description that is worded well enough to be understood

One system I use yt-dlp on is a FreeBSD home server. A FreeBSD installation of yt-dlp is less capable than a Linux installation because curl_cffi doesn't support FreeBSD ([open issue](https://github.com/lexiforest/curl_cffi/issues/365)). The [wreq](https://github.com/0x676e67/wreq-python) library for Python is an HTTP client similar to curl_cffi. It can impersonate browsers with customizable TLS, JA3/JA4, and HTTP/2 fingerprints.

wreq is implemented in Rust and is easy to build on FreeBSD. I would like yt-dlp to support wreq as an installation option. This way FreeBSD users will have a curl_cffi-style HTTP client.

### Provide verbose output that clearly demonstrates the problem

  * Run **your** yt-dlp command with **-vU** flag added (`yt-dlp -vU <your command line>`)
  * If using API, add `'verbose': True` to `YoutubeDL` params instead
  * Copy the WHOLE output (starting with `[debug] Command-line config`) and insert it below



### Complete Verbose Output

### Please make sure the question is worded well enough to be understood

### Checklist

  * I'm requesting a site-specific feature
  * I've verified that I have **updated yt-dlp to nightly or master** ([update instructions](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp#update-channels))
  * I've checked that all provided URLs are playable in a browser with the same IP and same login details
  * I've searched the [bugtracker](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues?q=is%3Aissue%20-label%3Aspam%20%20) for similar requests **including closed ones**. DO NOT post duplicates
  * I've read the [policy against AI/LLM contributions](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#automated-contributions-ai--llm-policy) and understand I may be blocked from the repository if it is violated
  * I've read about [sharing account credentials](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#are-you-willing-to-share-account-details-if-needed) and I'm willing to share it if required



### Region

_No response_

### Example URLs

<http://videa.hu/videok/allatok/az-orult-kigyasz-285-kigyot-kigyo-8YfIAjxwWGwT8HVQ>  
<https://videa.hu/videok/origo-auto/jarmuvek/gymkhana-2025-drift-subaru-bWvCTKUVNCan2Owq>

### Provide a description that is worded well enough to be understood

Currently the Videa extractor does not extract description, uploader or upload date.  
These fields are available in the player XML response (description, uploader_name) and in the JSON-LD VideoObject on the video webpage (uploadDate).

### Provide verbose output that clearly demonstrates the problem

  * Run **your** yt-dlp command with **-vU** flag added (`yt-dlp -vU <your command line>`)
  * If using API, add `'verbose': True` to `YoutubeDL` params instead
  * Copy the WHOLE output (starting with `[debug] Command-line config`) and insert it below

### Checklist

  * I'm requesting a site-specific feature
  * I've verified that I have **updated yt-dlp to nightly or master** ([update instructions](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp#update-channels))
  * I've checked that all provided URLs are playable in a browser with the same IP and same login details
  * I've searched the [bugtracker](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues?q=is%3Aissue%20-label%3Aspam%20%20) for similar requests **including closed ones**. DO NOT post duplicates
  * I've read the [policy against AI/LLM contributions](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#automated-contributions-ai--llm-policy) and understand I may be blocked from the repository if it is violated
  * I've read about [sharing account credentials](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#are-you-willing-to-share-account-details-if-needed) and I'm willing to share it if required



### Region

Germany

### Example URLs

Hey.  
<https://www.ardmediathek.de/mdr/elefanttigerundco>

### Provide a description that is worded well enough to be understood

Hey.

For the German public state TV ARD, there are pages like:
    
    
    https://www.ardmediathek.de/sendung/giraffe-erdmaennchen-und-co/Y3JpZDovL2hyLW9ubGluZS8zODIxMDI2NQ
    

which contain a whole programme (with all series and episodes) and which is already supported by yt-dlp (i.e. running it with that URL will download all episodes).

However there are also pages like:
    
    
    https://www.ardmediathek.de/mdr/elefanttigerundco
    

which is effectively the same (i.e. also a page with all episodes for a certain programme (here "Elefant, Tiger und Co.", but for these downloads don't work.

I tried to find a corresponding link of the form `https://www.ardmediathek.de/sendung/<programm-name>/<some-ID-or-code>`, but it seems that doesn't exist.

Would be nice if the other URL format could also be supported (and cause all episodes in it to be downloaded).

Thanks,  
Philippe.

### Provide verbose output that clearly demonstrates the problem

  * Run **your** yt-dlp command with **-vU** flag added (`yt-dlp -vU <your command line>`)
  * If using API, add `'verbose': True` to `YoutubeDL` params instead
  * Copy the WHOLE output (starting with `[debug] Command-line config`) and insert it below



### Complete Verbose Output
    
    
    doesn't really matter... it falls back to the generic extractor

### Example URLs

<https://vkvideo.ru/clip-211282506_456240577>  
<https://vk.com/clip-211282506_456240577>

### Provide a description that is worded well enough to be understood

\--embed-thumbnail gets a thumbnail with black borders when downloading clips.

Apparently the extractor used this link for embedding:
    
    
    https://sun9-11.userapi.com/impg/U-4x0GPMyBN8NbVM6Jx_7cZ_47M8WHkJ1awcRw/vGbjryzH69Y.jpg?size=800x450&quality=95&keep_aspect_ratio=1&background=000000&sign=a89d87324cfd5975019bad53516c7193&c_uniq_tag=LG4wzhQIKZ6uoDeu8VLtaoyy95N9jGQwwDGYPAJ1GvA&type=video_thumb
    

We can clean this link (and others) to get an image without transformations:
    
    
    https://sun9-11.userapi.com/U-4x0GPMyBN8NbVM6Jx_7cZ_47M8WHkJ1awcRw/vGbjryzH69Y.jpg
    

Now we have a proper image. Maybe this cleaning should be implemented in extractor. This will also be good for regular rectangular videos, because it will embed bigger images.

### Provide verbose output that clearly demonstrates the problem

  * Run **your** yt-dlp command with **-vU** flag added (`yt-dlp -vU <your command line>`)
  * If using API, add `'verbose': True` to `YoutubeDL` params instead
  * Copy the WHOLE output (starting with `[debug] Command-line config`) and insert it below

# [YouTube] Add output field for unique identifier for collaborators #16399

[YouTube] Add output field for unique identifier for collaborators#16399

Copy link

Labels

[site-enhancementFeature request for some website](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues?q=state%3Aopen%20label%3A%22site-enhancement%22)Feature request for some website[site:youtube](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues?q=state%3Aopen%20label%3A%22site%3Ayoutube%22)

[](https://github.com/Odd-Pianist3487)

## Description

[](https://github.com/Odd-Pianist3487)

[Odd-Pianist3487](https://github.com/Odd-Pianist3487)

opened [on Mar 31, 2026](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/16399#issue-4179708314)

Issue body actions

### Checklist

  * I'm requesting a site-specific feature
  * I've verified that I have **updated yt-dlp to nightly or master** ([update instructions](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp#update-channels))
  * I've checked that all provided URLs are playable in a browser with the same IP and same login details
  * I've searched the [bugtracker](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues?q=is%3Aissue%20-label%3Aspam%20%20) for similar requests **including closed ones**. DO NOT post duplicates
  * I've read the [policy against AI/LLM contributions](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#automated-contributions-ai--llm-policy) and understand I may be blocked from the repository if it is violated
  * I've read about [sharing account credentials](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#are-you-willing-to-share-account-details-if-needed) and I'm willing to share it if required



### Region

USA

### Example URLs

<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=El2ulWpN-pk>

### Provide a description that is worded well enough to be understood

There is currently no yt-dlp output field that identifies a collaborators clearly. There is `creator` and `creators`, but these just give the name of the collaborator channel that the creator can freely choose and for which there may be multiple channels which may have the same name which means that if the original video gets taken down for some reason, there is no way to say with certainty who the collaborator was because there might be many channels with the same name. To identify the collaborator clearly, there should be an output field which gives, if available, the collaborator YouTube channel ID (UC...) and/or an output field which gives, if available, the collaborator handle (@...) which are both unique per YouTube channel.

### Provide verbose output that clearly demonstrates the problem

  * Run **your** yt-dlp command with **-vU** flag added (`yt-dlp -vU <your command line>`)
  * If using API, add `'verbose': True` to `YoutubeDL` params instead
  * Copy the WHOLE output (starting with `[debug] Command-line config`) and insert it below



### Complete Verbose Output
    
    
    This is a site feature request to add one or two yt-dlp output fields for which I cannot give any yt-dlp verbose debug output because this is something to add as a feature and not a bug or something like that which needs yt-dlp verbose debug output.

Reactions are currently unavailable

### Example URLs

<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=f4YwpciOb8c> (Comment by `@Pasu4` contains italic, bold and strikethrough)  
<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Qy4agD90vy4> (Comment by `@Pasu4` contains nested style ranges)

### Provide a description that is worded well enough to be understood

Currently, the YouTube extractor only extracts the unstyled text of comments. For example, a comment written as "_Lorem_ *ipsum* -dolor-" (displayed as "_Lorem_ **ipsum** ~~dolor~~ ") is returned as "Lorem ipsum dolor" with the styling characters removed. It would be useful to also be able to additionally get the original text of the comment containing these styling characters, or if that is not possible, the style ranges. Looking at the the output of running with `--write-comments --dump-json`, no such information is returned, and there seems to be no command line argument or downloader argument that enables it.

## Use case

I use yt-dlp to fetch a comment containing timestamps from a video for [Pasu4/vedal-subathon-info](https://github.com/Pasu4/vedal-subathon-info). I want to convert the comment into Markdown, however, since yt-dlp only returns unstyled text, this is not possible using only yt-dlp. Currently I use the YouTube API as a replacement as it is able to return the original comment text with the styling characters present, but it requires a token, which may deter potential contributors.

## Investigation

By looking at the data returned from requests when loading the video, I was able to find an array of style ranges, located in the same object I believe the comment text is extracted from. The jq path for this array is (in my case) `.frameworkUpdates.entityBatchUpdate.mutations.[1].payload.commentEntityPayload.properties.content.styleRuns` (the comment text is extracted from `.frameworkUpdates.entityBatchUpdate.mutations.[1].payload.commentEntityPayload.properties.content.content`). Through debugging I confirmed that this property is accessible in the [`_extract_comment`](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/blob/2c28ee5d76d2c0d350407fd81dbdd71394b67993/yt_dlp/extractor/youtube/_video.py#L2383) method.

The objects contained in the `styleRuns` array have the following properties (purely based on observation):

  * `startIndex`: The character the range starts at.
  * `length`: The length of the range.
  * `weightLabel`: Either `"FONT_WEIGHT_NORMAL"` (normal) or `"FONT_WEIGHT_MEDIUM"` (bold)
  * `strikethrough`: Either `"LINE_STYLE_SINGLE"` or undefined (i.e. the property is not present in the object)
  * `italic`: Either `true` or undefined



Additional observations:

  * There may be sections of text in the comment that are not covered by a styling range, these are styled normally.
  * Styling ranges do not seem to overlap. "*_Hello_ World*" ("**_Hello_ World**") would result in two styling ranges ("Hello" and " World").
  * Timestamps have a styling range even though it does not change the style.

I also found a property that contains the original comment text with styling characters preserved (jq: `.frameworkUpdates.entityBatchUpdate.mutations.[4].payload.engagementToolbarSurfaceEntityPayload.menuCommand.innertubeCommand.menuEndpoint.menu.menuRenderer.items.[0].menuNavigationItemRenderer.navigationEndpoint.updateCommentDialogEndpoint.dialog.commentDialogRenderer.editableText.runs.[0].text`), however, it seems to only exists for comments written by myself.

## Proposed solutions

  1. Generate equivalent styling characters that would result in the same styling, but may not exactly match the original.  
Proposed example output: 
         
         {
           // ...
           "comments": [
             {
               "id": "UgzhAXXpHfr6zuVlVy54AaABAg",
               "parent": "root",
               "text": "00:00:00 Symphony — Clean Bandit\n00:03:27 Rolling Girl — wowaka\n00:06:37 Neuro appears | Just chatting\n00:18:45 Playing Legally Distinct •••dle\n00:19:43 Playing Legally Distinct Connections\n00:21:15 Playing Minesweeper (5x5, 5 mines)\n00:22:33 10x10, 5 mines\n01:16:55 Art review\n01:36:50 3D stream\n02:19:54 Raiding Shylily",
               "styledText": "00:00:00 _Symphony — Clean Bandit_\n00:03:27 _Rolling Girl — wowaka_\n00:06:37 Neuro appears | *Just chatting*\n00:18:45 Playing _Legally Distinct •••dle_\n00:19:43 Playing _Legally Distinct Connections_\n00:21:15 Playing _Minesweeper_ (5x5, 5 mines)\n00:22:33 10x10, 5 mines\n01:16:55 *Art review*\n01:36:50 *3D stream*\n02:19:54 Raiding Shylily",
               // ...
             },
             // ...
           ],
           // ...
         }

  2. Add the `styleRuns` property to the output JSON, maybe renamed and the elements converted to have booleans for bold, italic and strikethrough.  
Proposed example output: 
         
         {

## Description

[](https://github.com/coder0107git)

opened [on Mar 28, 2026](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/16363#issue-4156947583)

Issue body actions

### Checklist

  * I'm requesting a site-specific feature
  * I've verified that I have **updated yt-dlp to nightly or master** ([update instructions](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp#update-channels))
  * I've checked that all provided URLs are playable in a browser with the same IP and same login details
  * I've searched the [bugtracker](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues?q=is%3Aissue%20-label%3Aspam%20%20) for similar requests **including closed ones**. DO NOT post duplicates
  * I've read the [policy against AI/LLM contributions](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#automated-contributions-ai--llm-policy) and understand I may be blocked from the repository if it is violated
  * I've read about [sharing account credentials](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#are-you-willing-to-share-account-details-if-needed) and I'm willing to share it if required



### Region

United States

### Example URLs

  * Embedded video player: `https://www.youtubeeducation.com/embed/n_lqtqsXzkM`
  * Single video: `https://www.youtubeeducation.com/watch?v=n_lqtqsXzkM`
    * **Note:** These links are generated by the embedded video player, but seem to always result in 404s when visited. Quite likely a setup problem on YouTube's side.



### Provide a description that is worded well enough to be understood

On GSuite for Education accounts an alternative domain (`youtubeeducation.com`) is used by Google products to embed YouTube videos. Right now, it's not recognized as a YouTube link and just trust to use the generic downloader.

As far as I can tell, the only differences between `https://www.youtubeeducation.com/` and `https://www.youtube.com/` are that:

  * the domain is switched out
  * and the `https://www.youtubeeducation.com/` links only seem to have a functional embedded video player.



I think it would be simplest just to alias `https://www.youtubeeducation.com/` with the regular YouTube site.

### Provide verbose output that clearly demonstrates the problem

  * Run **your** yt-dlp command with **-vU** flag added (`yt-dlp -vU <your command line>`)
  * If using API, add `'verbose': True` to `YoutubeDL` params instead
  * Copy the WHOLE output (starting with `[debug] Command-line config`) and insert it below

However, it seems that yt-dlp does not support them.

### Region

United States

### Example URLs

<https://odysee.com/@Mantega:1/First-day-LBRY:1>

### Provide a description that is worded well enough to be understood

When downloading from YouTube, the `formats -> fragments` field is populated with thumbnails from the video. This is useful for efficiently displaying thumbnails in external applications (e.g. mpv w/ thumbfast/mpv_thumbnail_script). On Odysee thumbnails are stored as sprite sheets with a `vtt` file mapping each thumbnail range to its corresponding sprite sheet (with the required geometry). The `vtt` file itself is located at a similar location to the `m3u8` file after redirects are followed from the video.

Something like this sketch could be used as a starting point (somewhere in `yt_dlp/extractor/lbry.py` after the HEAD request is made to the video file):
    
    
    fragment_base_url = os.path.dirname(urlh.url)
    stream_sprite, _ = self._download_webpage_handle(
        os.path.join(fragment_base_url, 'stream_sprite.vtt'),
        display_id, 'Downloading stream thumbnails', headers=headers, fatal=False)
    format = {
        'fragments': [
            {
                'path': match.group(1),
                'duration': 2,
                'geometry': {
                    'x': int(match.group(2)),
                    'y': int(match.group(3)),
                    'w': int(match.group(4)),
                    'h': int(match.group(5)),
                }
            }
            for match in re.finditer(r'^\./(stream-[0-9]+.webp)#xywh=([0-9]+),([0-9]+),([0-9]+),([0-9]+)$', stream_sprite, re.MULTILINE)
        ],
        'fragment_base_url': fragment_base_url,
    }

For reference, the corresponding logic the webpage uses to fetch thumbnails is located in `ui/component/viewers/videoViewer/internal/videojs.jsx:587` under the site's webpack file. The thumbnails themselves are handled by `videojs-vtt-thumbnails`.

### Provide verbose output that clearly demonstrates the problem

  * Run **your** yt-dlp command with **-vU** flag added (`yt-dlp -vU <your command line>`)
  * If using API, add `'verbose': True` to `YoutubeDL` params instead
  * Copy the WHOLE output (starting with `[debug] Command-line config`) and insert it below

### Provide a description that is worded well enough to be understood

## Problem Description

When using `--download-archive` with Bilibili multi-part videos (选集), yt-dlp creates archive entries with `_p1`, `_p2`, etc. suffixes (e.g., `bilibili BV1M84y127mg_p1`). This causes two significant problems:

  1. **Inefficient duplicate detection** : When re-downloading the same playlist, yt-dlp fails to recognize already downloaded parts because it treats these suffixed IDs as monolithic identifiers, requiring re-parsing of all parts despite them already being in the archive.
  2. **Cannot detect playlist updates** : If new parts are added to an existing playlist, the archive mechanism cannot detect them because: 
     * The archive contains only individual suffixed entries (`_p1`, `_p2`, `_p3`).
     * The playlist URL (without suffixes) has no corresponding archive entry.
     * New parts (e.g., `_p4`) aren't in the archive, but yt-dlp doesn't know to check for them.



## Proposed Solution

Enhance yt-dlp's archive handling to parse and normalize Bilibili multi-part video IDs.

  1. When encountering a Bilibili URL ending in a base ID (without `_pN`), parse it to extract the base ID.
  2. Check the archive for any entries matching `baseID_p*`.
  3. Treat these as a single logical unit for the purpose of duplicate detection and update checking.



## Example Workflow

Initial state: Archive contains  
bilibili BV1M84y127mg_p1  
bilibili BV1M84y127mg_p2  
bilibili BV1M84y127mg_p3  
User runs:  
yt-dlp --download-archive archive.txt "<https://www.bilibili.com/video/BV1M84y127mg>"

yt-dlp behavior with proposed solution:  
Parse URL → base ID: BV1M84y127mg

Check archive → finds parts p1, p2, p3 for this base ID

Fetch playlist → discovers parts p1, p2, p3, p4 (newly added!)

Skip p1-p3 (already in archive)

Download only p4

Add to archive: bilibili BV1M84y127mg_p4

## Benefits

  * **Eliminates redundant downloads** : Already downloaded parts are skipped even when the URL is a base playlist link.
  * **Enables playlist updates** : New parts added to a Bilibili playlist are automatically detected and downloaded.
  * **Backward compatible** : Existing archive entries remain valid; the change only enhances interpretation.
  * **Simplifies user experience** : Users can use the base video URL without needing to manually specify individual part numbers.

I was unable to verify that the podcast is playable in a web browser, but I thought I should file this report regardless, in case yt-dlp wants to add safeguards against catastrophic loops, generally speaking.

possibly related: [#4752](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/4752)

# [Youtube] Request for update of --datebefore --dateafter behaviour when downloading videos chronologically via channels. #11084

New issue

Copy link

New issue

Copy link

Open

Open

[Youtube] Request for update of --datebefore --dateafter behaviour when downloading videos chronologically via channels.#11084

Copy link

Labels

[questionQuestion](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues?q=state%3Aopen%20label%3A%22question%22)Question[site:youtube](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues?q=state%3Aopen%20label%3A%22site%3Ayoutube%22)

[](https://github.com/pxssy)

## Description

[](https://github.com/pxssy)

[pxssy](https://github.com/pxssy)

opened [on Sep 25, 2024](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/11084#issue-2547768578)

Issue body actions

### DO NOT REMOVE OR SKIP THE ISSUE TEMPLATE

  * I understand that I will be **blocked** if I _intentionally_ remove or skip any mandatory* field



### Checklist

  * I'm requesting a site-specific feature
  * I've verified that I have **updated yt-dlp to nightly or master** ([update instructions](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp#update-channels))
  * I've checked that all provided URLs are playable in a browser with the same IP and same login details
  * I've searched [known issues](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/3766) and the [bugtracker](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues?q=) for similar issues **including closed ones**. DO NOT post duplicates
  * I've read the [guidelines for opening an issue](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#opening-an-issue)
  * I've read about [sharing account credentials](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#are-you-willing-to-share-account-details-if-needed) and I'm willing to share it if required



### Region

Singapore

### Example URLs

<https://www.youtube.com/@NileRed>

### Provide a description that is worded well enough to be understood

When a youtube channel input like <https://www.youtube.com/@NileRed> is given to yt-dlp, it parses ALL /video and /shorts, then downloads them sequentially by chronological order, latest upload first, as its what is given by the API. Its not possible to sort in any other way.

In this case, If an option like --dateafter or --datebefore is used, many unnecessary requests are sent to youtube for videos that clearly will not match a filter.

Example

yt-dlp <https://www.youtube.com/@NileRed> \--dateafter 21001231 will match 0 videos, since the earliest video is in 2024. However it will check through EVERY video, even the ones before 2024, which is unnecessary and slow.

Similarly, yt-dlp <https://www.youtube.com/@NileRed> \--datebefore 00010101 will also match 0 videos, but it will check every video until the very first one.

Until youtube changes this, I believe this additional checks are not necessary at all.

Therefore I suggest 2 changes.

  1. \--datebefore runs the downloading backwards, starting from the oldest video in the channel.



EDIT: an existing workaround is -I "::-1"

  2. a switch like --date-skip 5, that skips process after it has checked 5 videos and they do not match the date requirements.



Expected behaviour should then be

yt-dlp <https://www.youtube.com/@NileRed> \--dateafter 20240101 --date-skip 3

Downloads videos after 20240101  
skip  
skip  
skip  
Download shorts after 20240101  
skip  
skip  
skip

exit

### Provide verbose output that clearly demonstrates the problem

  * Run **your** yt-dlp command with **-vU** flag added (`yt-dlp -vU <your command line>`)
  * If using API, add `'verbose': True` to `YoutubeDL` params instead
  * Copy the WHOLE output (starting with `[debug] Command-line config`) and insert it below

Extractors: Availability of DOM query functions#10621

Copy link

Labels

[questionQuestion](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues?q=state%3Aopen%20label%3A%22question%22)Question

## Description

[](https://github.com/Lalufu)

[Lalufu](https://github.com/Lalufu)

opened [on Aug 1, 2024](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/10621#issue-2442230799)

Issue body actions

### DO NOT REMOVE OR SKIP THE ISSUE TEMPLATE

  * I understand that I will be **blocked** if I _intentionally_ remove or skip any mandatory* field



### Checklist

  * I'm asking a question and **not** reporting a bug or requesting a feature
  * I've looked through the [README](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp#readme)
  * I've verified that I have **updated yt-dlp to nightly or master** ([update instructions](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp#update-channels))
  * I've searched [known issues](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/3766) and the [bugtracker](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues?q=) for similar questions **including closed ones**. DO NOT post duplicates
  * I've read the [guidelines for opening an issue](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#opening-an-issue)



### Please make sure the question is worded well enough to be understood

I am looking into writing a new extractor, and I'm wondering if I'm missing some obvious utility functions for extracting information from a HTML page. I had, maybe naively, expected there to be functions similar to `document.querySelector()` and `document.querySelectorAll()` from JS, which take a more or less abstract path through the document and return matching elements, maybe backed by `BeautifulSoup` or other libraries. I have found the `get_element_*` functions from `utils`, which don't seem to quite do the same thing (I can't seem to look for tags of a certain type?), and looking at other extractors, using regular expressions seems to be pretty popular for some reason instead. There's also some xpath support, but from a quick look nothing seems to utilize this for dealing with HTML.  
Do functions like this exist, and I haven't found them, or is this a discouraged approach for some reason?

### Provide verbose output that clearly demonstrates the problem

  * Run **your** yt-dlp command with **-vU** flag added (`yt-dlp -vU <your command line>`)
  * If using API, add `'verbose': True` to `YoutubeDL` params instead
  * Copy the WHOLE output (starting with `[debug] Command-line config`) and insert it below



### Complete Verbose Output

### Checklist

  * I'm reporting that yt-dlp is broken on a **supported** site
  * I've verified that I have **updated yt-dlp to nightly or master** ([update instructions](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp#update-channels))
  * I've checked that all provided URLs are playable in a browser with the same IP and same login details
  * I've checked that all URLs and arguments with special characters are [properly quoted or escaped](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/wiki/FAQ#video-url-contains-an-ampersand--and-im-getting-some-strange-output-1-2839-or-v-is-not-recognized-as-an-internal-or-external-command)
  * I've searched [known issues](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/3766), [the FAQ](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/wiki/FAQ), and the [bugtracker](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues?q=is%3Aissue%20-label%3Aspam%20%20) for similar issues **including closed ones**. DO NOT post duplicates
  * I've read the [policy against AI/LLM contributions](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#automated-contributions-ai--llm-policy) and understand I may be blocked from the repository if it is violated
  * I've read about [sharing account credentials](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#are-you-willing-to-share-account-details-if-needed) and I'm willing to share it if required



### Region

USA

### Provide a description that is worded well enough to be understood

Using --cookies-from-browser results in Requested format is not available. If I remove the --cookies-from-browser it downloads OK.

### Provide verbose output that clearly demonstrates the problem

  * Run **your** yt-dlp command with **-vU** flag added (`yt-dlp -vU <your command line>`)
  * If using API, add `'verbose': True` to `YoutubeDL` params instead
  * Copy the WHOLE output (starting with `[debug] Command-line config`) and insert it below

Having yt-dlp create a symlink for playlists with a certain path#13674

Copy link

Labels

[questionQuestion](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues?q=state%3Aopen%20label%3A%22question%22)Question

[](https://github.com/Aces-and-Jacks)

## Description

[](https://github.com/Aces-and-Jacks)

[Aces-and-Jacks](https://github.com/Aces-and-Jacks)

opened [on Jul 9, 2025](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/13674#issue-3214340349)

Issue body actions

### Checklist

  * I'm asking a question and **not** reporting a bug or requesting a feature
  * I've looked through the [README](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp#readme)
  * I've verified that I have **updated yt-dlp to nightly or master** ([update instructions](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp#update-channels))
  * I've searched [known issues](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/3766), [the FAQ](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/wiki/FAQ), and the [bugtracker](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues?q=is%3Aissue%20-label%3Aspam%20%20) for similar questions **including closed ones**. DO NOT post duplicates



### Please make sure the question is worded well enough to be understood

As far as I can see, no one has posted a question like this. I know you can use the `--exec` command for symlinks. But I'm not really code savy to figure this out. This probably isn't possible but I figured it wouldn't hurt to ask.

I currently have the videos I download symlinked as `--exec 'cd "/Users/$USER/Downloads/sym-folder" && ln -s --'`. Which worked well before. All my videoes get downloaded to their own folders as `/Users/$USER/YT-Downloads/%(uploader)s-[%(uploader_id)s]/%(uploader)s-%(upload_date>%Y-%m-%d)s_%(title)s-[%(id)s]/%(uploader)s-%(upload_date)s_%(title)s-[%(id)s].%(ext)s'` and the resulting files get symlinked to the other directory.

The thing is when I download a playlist, a folder that shows the playlist uploader gets created along with the other uploads for each video `%(uploader)s-[%(uploader_id)s]`. Which I'm fine with (I also see in the info file the playlist name and count it was with), but for the symlinked videos they just show without any filepath order. Which would make sense based on the file path. I tried using one of the fields in the OUTPUT TEMPLATE options but that didn't work properly. I figured it probably wouldn't tho.

I had asked for help for just symlinking in the past in [#11080](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/11080) and based on what `bashonly` provided I tried to figure it out. He mentioned there was a field for `filepath` but I guess I had asked too many questions since he didn't answer, and I had already gotten my main question at the time answered. For symlinking he meantioned

> `ln -s -- %(filepath,_filename|)q`

but then said

> IMPORTANT: you should only ever use `%()q` in `--exec` arguments, and never `%()s`

So to sum it all up, I was wondering about a command that creates symlinks in a filepath that includes the playlist uploader. Like some sort of field string or something. I hope I didn't make this too confusing.

### Provide verbose output that clearly demonstrates the problem

  * Run **your** yt-dlp command with **-vU** flag added (`yt-dlp -vU <your command line>`)
  * If using API, add `'verbose': True` to `YoutubeDL` params instead
  * Copy the WHOLE output (starting with `[debug] Command-line config`) and insert it below

## Description

[](https://github.com/Pomato1999)

[Pomato1999](https://github.com/Pomato1999)

opened [on Apr 24, 2026](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/16568#issue-4320126748)

Issue body actions

### Checklist

  * I'm asking a question and **not** reporting a bug or requesting a feature
  * I've looked through the [README](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp#readme)
  * I've verified that I have **updated yt-dlp to nightly or master** ([update instructions](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp#update-channels))
  * I've searched [known issues](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/3766), [the FAQ](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/wiki/FAQ), and the [bugtracker](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues?q=is%3Aissue%20-label%3Aspam%20%20) for similar questions **including closed ones**. DO NOT post duplicates
  * I've read the [policy against AI/LLM contributions](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#automated-contributions-ai--llm-policy) and understand I may be blocked from the repository if it is violated



### Please make sure the question is worded well enough to be understood

When using --force-keyframes-at-cuts, I found that this parameter invokes ffmpeg for re-encoding, which is extremely CPU-intensive. Additionally, I have multiple processes downloading, and since the re-encoding process of ffmpeg depends on the number of physical cores, assuming my server only has 4 physical cores, how can I force the re-encoding of a single process to only use one physical core, in order to reduce the scheduling overhead between processes? Is there such a method?

### Provide verbose output that clearly demonstrates the problem

  * Run **your** yt-dlp command with **-vU** flag added (`yt-dlp -vU <your command line>`)
  * If using API, add `'verbose': True` to `YoutubeDL` params instead
  * Copy the WHOLE output (starting with `[debug] Command-line config`) and insert it below



### Complete Verbose Output

## Description

[](https://github.com/dajotim937)

[dajotim937](https://github.com/dajotim937)

opened [on Jun 3, 2025](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/13381#issue-3113644843)

Issue body actions

### Checklist

  * I'm reporting a bug unrelated to a specific site
  * I've verified that I have **updated yt-dlp to nightly or master** ([update instructions](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp#update-channels))
  * I've searched [known issues](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/3766), [the FAQ](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/wiki/FAQ), and the [bugtracker](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues?q=is%3Aissue%20-label%3Aspam%20%20) for similar issues **including closed ones**. DO NOT post duplicates



### Provide a description that is worded well enough to be understood

So, here is related issue: [#6501](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/6501)

But I'm asking not about overwriting original video file, but about final (opus in case of youtube) file that being overwritten.

Example:  
`yt-dlp.exe -f bestaudio --extract-audio --audio-quality 0 --parse-metadata "%(uploader)s:%(meta_channelName)s" --embed-metadata -o "%(title)s.%(ext)s" https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=OcrsSaWZ4CY`  
This command download video and extract audio into 'Deja Reve.opus' file.  
Then:  
`yt-dlp.exe -f bestaudio --extract-audio --audio-quality 0 --parse-metadata "%(uploader)s:%(meta_channelName)s" --embed-metadata --no-overwrites "%(title)s.%(ext)s" -w https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=L8M71Xu1rVc`  
And no warnings, no errors, just overwrite of final file.

Well, it's kinda hard to tell from first glance. Same track with same name and maybe yt-dlp just overwrite metadata.  
`yt-dlp.exe -f bestaudio --extract-audio --audio-quality 0 --parse-metadata "%(uploader)s:%(meta_channelName)s" --embed-metadata -o "%(title)s.%(ext)s" https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=zIAku-Qwfl0`  
`yt-dlp.exe -f bestaudio --extract-audio --audio-quality 0 --parse-metadata "%(uploader)s:%(meta_channelName)s" --embed-metadata -o "%(title)s.%(ext)s" --no-overwrites https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=cBQpZsnLyMw`

Yeah, nope. End up with second track that overwrite first one. So. Is it a bug? Or intended behaviour? How to prevent such behaviour if so (except puting something like %(id)s into filename)?

### Provide verbose output that clearly demonstrates the problem

  * Run **your** yt-dlp command with **-vU** flag added (`yt-dlp -vU <your command line>`)
  * If using API, add `'verbose': True` to `YoutubeDL` params instead
  * Copy the WHOLE output (starting with `[debug] Command-line config`) and insert it below

# [TikTok] TikTok Web extractor ignores bitrateInfo.PlayAddr.Width/Height and incorrectly maps some 540p formats to 576x1024 #16532
