[TikTok] TikTok Web extractor ignores bitrateInfo.PlayAddr.Width/Height and incorrectly maps some 540p formats to 576x1024#16532

Copy link

Labels

[site-bugIssue with a specific website](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues?q=state%3Aopen%20label%3A%22site-bug%22)Issue with a specific website

[](https://github.com/Index103000)

## Description

[](https://github.com/Index103000)

[Index103000](https://github.com/Index103000)

opened [on Apr 20, 2026](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/16532#issue-4295235530)

Issue body actions

### Checklist

  * I'm reporting a bug unrelated to a specific site
  * I've verified that I have **updated yt-dlp to nightly or master** ([update instructions](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp#update-channels))
  * I've searched [known issues](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/3766), [the FAQ](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/wiki/FAQ), and the [bugtracker](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues?q=is%3Aissue%20-label%3Aspam%20%20) for similar issues **including closed ones**. DO NOT post duplicates
  * I've read the [policy against AI/LLM contributions](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#automated-contributions-ai--llm-policy) and understand I may be blocked from the repository if it is violated



### Provide a description that is worded well enough to be understood

For some TikTok videos, the Web extractor derives the format resolution from `PlayAddr.UrlKey` and applies the hardcoded rule:
    
    
    if dimension == 540:  # '540p' is actually 576p
        dimension = 576

This works for some videos, but it is not always correct.

In some Web JSON responses, bitrateInfo.PlayAddr already contains explicit Width and Height fields. For these videos, the extractor currently ignores those fields and derives width / height from UrlKey + ratio instead.

As a result, some formats are reported as 576x1024 by yt-dlp, while TikTok’s own PlayAddr.Width/Height and the actual downloaded file are 540x960.

Example 1: 540p is actually 540x960

Video ID: 102363108337192960
    
    
    {
      "video": {
        "id": "102363108337192960",
        "width": 540,
        "height": 960,
        "ratio": "540p",
        "definition": "540p",
        "bitrateInfo": [
          {
            "Bitrate": 1041872,
            "GearName": "adapt_540_1",
            "PlayAddr": {
              "DataSize": "1847501",
              "Width": 540,
              "Height": 960,
              "UrlKey": "v0b044490000bo706aahv5vn4q05edv0_bytevc1_540p_1041872"
            },
            "CodecType": "h265_hvc1",
            "Format": "mp4"
          }
        ]
      }
    }

The downloaded file also reports 540x960

Example 2: 720p is actually 576x1024

Video ID: 6585786671671807238
    
    
    {
      "video": {
        "id": "6585786671671807238",
        "width": 576,
        "height": 1024,
        "ratio": "720p",
        "definition": "720p",
        "bitrateInfo": [
          {
            "Bitrate": 1258633,
            "GearName": "normal_720_0",
            "PlayAddr": {
              "DataSize": "2445150",
              "Width": 576,
              "Height": 1024,
              "UrlKey": "v090446c0000bdimjn89pog8ra75btp0_h264_720p_1258633"
            },
            "CodecType": "h264",
            "Format": "mp4"
          }
        ]
      }
    }
    

The downloaded file also reports 576x1024

Suggested fix

Prefer bitrateInfo.PlayAddr.Width and bitrateInfo.PlayAddr.Height when present, and only fall back to UrlKey + ratio inference when they are missing.

This keeps the existing fallback behavior for responses that do not include PlayAddr.Width/Height, while avoiding incorrect metadata when TikTok already provides explicit per-format dimensions.

### Provide verbose output that clearly demonstrates the problem

  * Run **your** yt-dlp command with **-vU** flag added (`yt-dlp -vU <your command line>`)
  * If using API, add `'verbose': True` to `YoutubeDL` params instead
  * Copy the WHOLE output (starting with `[debug] Command-line config`) and insert it below

### Provide a description that is worded well enough to be understood

with flv format, when the live ends, it returns error which prevents the conversion of `.flv.part` to `.flv`, and for the metadata to be applied accordingly.

this error first appeared about a week ago, but it has been inconsistent and doesn't happen to every profile.

### Provide verbose output that clearly demonstrates the problem

  * Run **your** yt-dlp command with **-vU** flag added (`yt-dlp -vU <your command line>`)
  * If using API, add `'verbose': True` to `YoutubeDL` params instead
  * Copy the WHOLE output (starting with `[debug] Command-line config`) and insert it below



### Complete Verbose Output
    
    
    [debug] Command-line config: ['-o', 'tiktok/%(uploader)s/[%(id)s] %(title)s.%(ext)s', '--write-info-json', '-v', '--no-embed-metadata', '--no-embed-info-json', '--xattrs', 'https://www.tiktok.com/@USERNAME/live', '-f', 'flv-origin', '--retries', '0']
    [debug] Encodings: locale UTF-8, fs utf-8, pref UTF-8, out utf-8, error utf-8, screen utf-8

### Checklist

  * I'm reporting that yt-dlp is broken on a **supported** site
  * I've verified that I have **updated yt-dlp to nightly or master** ([update instructions](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp#update-channels))
  * I've checked that all provided URLs are playable in a browser with the same IP and same login details
  * I've checked that all URLs and arguments with special characters are [properly quoted or escaped](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/wiki/FAQ#video-url-contains-an-ampersand--and-im-getting-some-strange-output-1-2839-or-v-is-not-recognized-as-an-internal-or-external-command)
  * I've searched [known issues](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/3766), [the FAQ](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/wiki/FAQ), and the [bugtracker](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues?q=is%3Aissue%20-label%3Aspam%20%20) for similar issues **including closed ones**. DO NOT post duplicates
  * I've read the [policy against AI/LLM contributions](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#automated-contributions-ai--llm-policy) and understand I may be blocked from the repository if it is violated
  * I've read about [sharing account credentials](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#are-you-willing-to-share-account-details-if-needed) and I'm willing to share it if required



### Region

_No response_

### Provide a description that is worded well enough to be understood

The extractor hits `http://svp.vg.no/...`, which now returns a 308 redirect to a Schibsted-internal edge host that silently drops TCP connections from public egress; fix seems to be updating that endpoint to use https instead (I do have a tiny PR ready for that).

### Provide verbose output that clearly demonstrates the problem

  * Run **your** yt-dlp command with **-vU** flag added (`yt-dlp -vU <your command line>`)
  * If using API, add `'verbose': True` to `YoutubeDL` params instead
  * Copy the WHOLE output (starting with `[debug] Command-line config`) and insert it below

  * I've read about [sharing account credentials](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#are-you-willing-to-share-account-details-if-needed) and I'm willing to share it if required



### Region

China

### Provide a description that is worded well enough to be understood

When attempting to use `--write-info-json` and `--write-subs` for fetching metadata and additional files of a video on Bilibili, the request fails if the URL doesn't start with `www.`.

For example, these commands work:
    
    
    $ yt-dlp --write-subs --no-download 'https://www.bilibili.com/video/BV1DYoSBAEoi'
    $ yt-dlp --write-info-json --no-download 'https://www.bilibili.com/video/BV1DYoSBAEoi'
    

But these don't:
    
    
    $ yt-dlp --write-subs --no-download 'https://bilibili.com/video/BV1DYoSBAEoi'
    $ yt-dlp --write-info-json --no-download 'https://bilibili.com/video/BV1DYoSBAEoi'
    

The latter commands fail with the error message (details logs are omitted here for clarify, see the end of this issue for full logs).
    
    
    [BiliBili] Extracting URL: https://bilibili.com/video/BV1DYoSBAEoi
    [BiliBili] 1DYoSBAEoi: Downloading webpage
    [BiliBili] BV1DYoSBAEoi: Extracting videos in anthology
    WARNING: [BiliBili] Unable to download JSON metadata: HTTP Error 403: Forbidden
    [BiliBili] BV1DYoSBAEoi: Downloading wbi sign
    [BiliBili] BV1DYoSBAEoi: Downloading video formats for cid 37813027890
    ERROR: [BiliBili] 1DYoSBAEoi: Unable to download JSON metadata: HTTP Error 403: Forbidden (caused by <HTTPError 403: Forbidden>)
    

Strangely, after a Pull Request [#16578](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/pull/16578) is applied (which fixes a challenge-response problem which doesn't have direct relationship with this issue), the 403 error for `--write-info-json` is also solved, which is surprising to both developers. After much digging, I was managed to isolate the root cause to an one line change:
    
    
    diff --git a/yt_dlp/extractor/bilibili.py b/yt_dlp/extractor/bilibili.py
    index 207d482..7e07a93 100644
    --- a/yt_dlp/extractor/bilibili.py
    +++ b/yt_dlp/extractor/bilibili.py
    @@ -662,7 +662,7 @@ def _real_extract(self, url):
             if not self._match_valid_url(urlh.url):
                 return self.url_result(urlh.url)
     
    -        headers['Referer'] = url
    +        headers['Referer'] = "https://www.bilibili.com"
     
             initial_state = self._search_json(r'window\.__INITIAL_STATE__\s*=', webpage, 'initial state', video_id, default=None)
             if not initial_state:

Thus, it seems that Bilibili's system is treating `www.bilibili.com` as the canonical domain name, not `bilibili.com`, a request with a `Referer` field using `bilibili.com` is now rejected via HTTP 403.

Furthermore, even after applying this fix, a separate error for `--write-subs` remains. This means we probably need to pass `Referer: https://www.bilibili.com` when downloading `https://comment.bilibili.com/$id.xml` as well.

This problem is reproducible both when logged out and logged in. For simplicity, only the logged-in case is tested here.

### Provide verbose output that clearly demonstrates the problem

  * Run **your** yt-dlp command with **-vU** flag added (`yt-dlp -vU <your command line>`)
  * If using API, add `'verbose': True` to `YoutubeDL` params instead
  * Copy the WHOLE output (starting with `[debug] Command-line config`) and insert it below

### Checklist

  * I'm reporting that yt-dlp is broken on a **supported** site
  * I've verified that I have **updated yt-dlp to nightly or master** ([update instructions](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp#update-channels))
  * I've checked that all provided URLs are playable in a browser with the same IP and same login details
  * I've checked that all URLs and arguments with special characters are [properly quoted or escaped](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/wiki/FAQ#video-url-contains-an-ampersand--and-im-getting-some-strange-output-1-2839-or-v-is-not-recognized-as-an-internal-or-external-command)
  * I've searched [known issues](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/3766), [the FAQ](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/wiki/FAQ), and the [bugtracker](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues?q=is%3Aissue%20-label%3Aspam%20%20) for similar issues **including closed ones**. DO NOT post duplicates
  * I've read the [policy against AI/LLM contributions](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#automated-contributions-ai--llm-policy) and understand I may be blocked from the repository if it is violated
  * I've read about [sharing account credentials](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#are-you-willing-to-share-account-details-if-needed) and I'm willing to share it if required



### Region

Pakistan

### Provide a description that is worded well enough to be understood

I am writing this issue that i parsed a file to yt-dlp that contained 140 links from a facebook page, yt-dlp performed very well and downloaded 120 of them but skipped 20 videos, and after implementing multiple pragmatic solutions it kept skipping those videos and then I read a message in the logs that was to ensure the usage of latest version and after that report the issue to this url:  
Cannot parse data; please report this issue on <https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues?q=> , filling out the appropriate issue template.

This was the message I got and I pasted it inside this issue, btw i don't know that much about issuing and it is my first ever issue creation, so I hope to get this issue done and also any better tip on how to be a good issue highlighter.

  * Run **your** yt-dlp command with **-vU** flag added (`yt-dlp -vU <your command line>`)
  * If using API, add `'verbose': True` to `YoutubeDL` params instead
  * Copy the WHOLE output (starting with `[debug] Command-line config`) and insert it below

# Some URLs on 10Play fallback to generic extractor then fail "Unsupported URL" #16541

Copy link

Labels

[site-bugIssue with a specific website](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues?q=state%3Aopen%20label%3A%22site-bug%22)Issue with a specific website[triageUntriaged issue](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues?q=state%3Aopen%20label%3A%22triage%22)Untriaged issue

[](https://github.com/section83)

## Description

[](https://github.com/section83)

[section83](https://github.com/section83)

opened [on Apr 21, 2026](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/16541#issue-4300469040)

Issue body actions

### Checklist

  * I'm reporting that yt-dlp is broken on a **supported** site
  * I've verified that I have **updated yt-dlp to nightly or master** ([update instructions](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp#update-channels))
  * I've checked that all provided URLs are playable in a browser with the same IP and same login details
  * I've checked that all URLs and arguments with special characters are [properly quoted or escaped](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/wiki/FAQ#video-url-contains-an-ampersand--and-im-getting-some-strange-output-1-2839-or-v-is-not-recognized-as-an-internal-or-external-command)
  * I've searched [known issues](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/3766), [the FAQ](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/wiki/FAQ), and the [bugtracker](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues?q=is%3Aissue%20-label%3Aspam%20%20) for similar issues **including closed ones**. DO NOT post duplicates
  * I've read the [policy against AI/LLM contributions](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#automated-contributions-ai--llm-policy) and understand I may be blocked from the repository if it is violated
  * I've read about [sharing account credentials](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#are-you-willing-to-share-account-details-if-needed) and I'm willing to share it if required



### Region

Australia

### Provide a description that is worded well enough to be understood

10Play in Australia uses very plain URLs for movies in this format. Those URLs are not processed by the 10Play extractor but instead are passed to the generic extractor which then reports the URL is not supported. An example URL is for the movie "Confess Fletch":
    
    
    10.com.au/confess-fletch
    

The 10Play yt-dlp extractor works normally for most 10Play URLs e.g.:
    
    
    https://10.com.au/titans-the-rise-of-wall-street/episodes/season-1/episode-2/tpv251205jbkvq
    

Can the shorter 10Play URLs be handled by the 10Play extractor ?

All 10Play downloads require credentials and are probably geoblocked. I use netrc to supply credentials.

### Provide verbose output that clearly demonstrates the problem

  * Run **your** yt-dlp command with **-vU** flag added (`yt-dlp -vU <your command line>`)
  * If using API, add `'verbose': True` to `YoutubeDL` params instead
  * Copy the WHOLE output (starting with `[debug] Command-line config`) and insert it below

### Checklist

  * I'm reporting that yt-dlp is broken on a **supported** site
  * I've verified that I have **updated yt-dlp to nightly or master** ([update instructions](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp#update-channels))
  * I've checked that all provided URLs are playable in a browser with the same IP and same login details
  * I've checked that all URLs and arguments with special characters are [properly quoted or escaped](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/wiki/FAQ#video-url-contains-an-ampersand--and-im-getting-some-strange-output-1-2839-or-v-is-not-recognized-as-an-internal-or-external-command)
  * I've searched [known issues](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/3766), [the FAQ](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/wiki/FAQ), and the [bugtracker](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues?q=is%3Aissue%20-label%3Aspam%20%20) for similar issues **including closed ones**. DO NOT post duplicates
  * I've read the [policy against AI/LLM contributions](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#automated-contributions-ai--llm-policy) and understand I may be blocked from the repository if it is violated
  * I've read about [sharing account credentials](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#are-you-willing-to-share-account-details-if-needed) and I'm willing to share it if required



### Region

Australia

### Provide a description that is worded well enough to be understood

SBS Ondemand was working fine with yt-dlp as recently as Sunday evening (AEST), but it now results in a "410: Gone" error. The SBS website has changed the url formats. Using both the new format and changing it back to the old format both result in the same 410 error.

### Provide verbose output that clearly demonstrates the problem

  * Run **your** yt-dlp command with **-vU** flag added (`yt-dlp -vU <your command line>`)
  * If using API, add `'verbose': True` to `YoutubeDL` params instead
  * Copy the WHOLE output (starting with `[debug] Command-line config`) and insert it below

### Checklist

  * I'm reporting that yt-dlp is broken on a **supported** site
  * I've verified that I have **updated yt-dlp to nightly or master** ([update instructions](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp#update-channels))
  * I've checked that all provided URLs are playable in a browser with the same IP and same login details
  * I've checked that all URLs and arguments with special characters are [properly quoted or escaped](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/wiki/FAQ#video-url-contains-an-ampersand--and-im-getting-some-strange-output-1-2839-or-v-is-not-recognized-as-an-internal-or-external-command)
  * I've searched [known issues](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/3766), [the FAQ](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/wiki/FAQ), and the [bugtracker](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues?q=is%3Aissue%20-label%3Aspam%20%20) for similar issues **including closed ones**. DO NOT post duplicates
  * I've read the [policy against AI/LLM contributions](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#automated-contributions-ai--llm-policy) and understand I may be blocked from the repository if it is violated
  * I've read about [sharing account credentials](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#are-you-willing-to-share-account-details-if-needed) and I'm willing to share it if required



### Region

no geo-restriction (to my knowledge)

### Provide a description that is worded well enough to be understood

Al-Jazeera is listed as a supported site in `yt-dlp --list-extractors` and in <https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/blob/master/supportedsites.md>

Yet, from the log, it appears that the [aljazeera] extractor is not used, but only the generic extractor, which fails.

I found no open issue for Al-Jazeera.

### Provide verbose output that clearly demonstrates the problem

  * Run **your** yt-dlp command with **-vU** flag added (`yt-dlp -vU <your command line>`)
  * If using API, add `'verbose': True` to `YoutubeDL` params instead
  * Copy the WHOLE output (starting with `[debug] Command-line config`) and insert it below

### Checklist

  * I'm reporting that yt-dlp is broken on a **supported** site
  * I've verified that I have **updated yt-dlp to nightly or master** ([update instructions](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp#update-channels))
  * I've checked that all provided URLs are playable in a browser with the same IP and same login details
  * I've checked that all URLs and arguments with special characters are [properly quoted or escaped](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/wiki/FAQ#video-url-contains-an-ampersand--and-im-getting-some-strange-output-1-2839-or-v-is-not-recognized-as-an-internal-or-external-command)
  * I've searched [known issues](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/3766), [the FAQ](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/wiki/FAQ), and the [bugtracker](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues?q=is%3Aissue%20-label%3Aspam%20%20) for similar issues **including closed ones**. DO NOT post duplicates
  * I've read the [policy against AI/LLM contributions](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#automated-contributions-ai--llm-policy) and understand I may be blocked from the repository if it is violated
  * I've read about [sharing account credentials](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#are-you-willing-to-share-account-details-if-needed) and I'm willing to share it if required



### Region

Japan

I'm running on Ubuntu 24.04 LTS

# Document setup of extras for non-PyPI installations #16224

Document setup of extras for non-PyPI installations#16224

Copy link

[](https://github.com/zahlman)

## Description

[](https://github.com/zahlman)

[zahlman](https://github.com/zahlman)

opened [on Mar 12, 2026](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/16224#issue-4066913711)

Issue body actions

### Checklist

  * I'm requesting a feature unrelated to a specific site
  * I've looked through the [README](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp#readme)
  * I've verified that I have **updated yt-dlp to nightly or master** ([update instructions](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp#update-channels))
  * I've searched the [bugtracker](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues?q=is%3Aissue%20-label%3Aspam%20%20) for similar requests **including closed ones**. DO NOT post duplicates
  * I've read the [policy against AI/LLM contributions](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#automated-contributions-ai--llm-policy) and understand I may be blocked from the repository if it is violated



### Provide a description that is worded well enough to be understood

I'm a Python developer, so I can easily set up `yt-dlp` in a virtual environment, add dependencies to that environment based on the dependency groups in `pyproject.toml`, etc. But most users aren't in that situation.

In places where yt-dlp is discussed (such as the Linux Mint forums) I come across a fair number of people who have installed yt-dlp either through a system package manager, the zipapp or a compiled all-in-one package, and then want to install some extra or other. For example, most recently someone wanted to use the impersonation feature, which per the main documentation requires `[curl-cffi]`, not included in the zipapp (since this was on the Mint forums, I can pretty safely rule out the MUSL binary).

I have noticed that the zipapp uses a `#!/usr/bin/env python3` shebang, so in principle a Linux user could activate a virtual environment where the extra dependencies are installed before using the `yt-dlp` command (and possibly also e.g. wrap those two steps in a Bash function), but that's a lot to expect of most people (including those who are now migrating to Linux as Win11 continues to annoy everyone).

Meanwhile I expect that most people will do some research, try to set up those dependencies in the system environment, run into PEP 668 protections and then pester support forums to decide what to do about those protections. Right now this project's documentation just tells people to e.g. `pip install "yt-dlp[default,curl-cffi]"`, without any consideration of the target environment.

It would be good to either:

  * Build a system into `yt-dlp` that lets it manage its own venv and put some dependencies there;

  * Document how users are intended to obtain these dependencies (even if they aren't accustomed to Python packaging) and establish a stance on whether to install them in the system environment (i.e. whether users are expected to use `--break-system-packages`, include a reference to some Python documentation of the trade-offs etc.)




Whatever you think is the right way to do things is fine by me; I know how to do it many ways anyway. But if you do have an opinion, other users should understand that opinion, and how to act on it.

Alternately, I could write up a PR to add multiple ways of doing it to the Installation section of the wiki. But I don't really know the best way to organize it. (I also have a shelved wiki project of my own, generally about "installing Python stuff", that I could resume and reference...)

### Provide verbose output that clearly demonstrates the problem

  * Run **your** yt-dlp command with **-vU** flag added (`yt-dlp -vU <your command line>`)
  * If using API, add `'verbose': True` to `YoutubeDL` params instead
  * Copy the WHOLE output (starting with `[debug] Command-line config`) and insert it below



### Complete Verbose Output
    
    
    Not applicable, as this is not about a specific problem from running the program (just documentation and/or simplification of the install process).

## Description

[](https://github.com/columndeeply)

[columndeeply](https://github.com/columndeeply)

opened [on Apr 19, 2026](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/16517#issue-4290126501)

Issue body actions

### Checklist

  * I'm requesting a feature unrelated to a specific site
  * I've looked through the [README](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp#readme)
  * I've verified that I have **updated yt-dlp to nightly or master** ([update instructions](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp#update-channels))
  * I've searched the [bugtracker](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues?q=is%3Aissue%20-label%3Aspam%20%20) for similar requests **including closed ones**. DO NOT post duplicates
  * I've read the [policy against AI/LLM contributions](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#automated-contributions-ai--llm-policy) and understand I may be blocked from the repository if it is violated



### Provide a description that is worded well enough to be understood

A way to trigger a command when a download fails or there's an error would be great. Right now I'm using "--exec" to get a notification each time a video downloads, but I have no way to get one when the download fails.

I have a script pull new videos from a list of channels, but I've missed videos because they were age restricted and the script was skipping them. If I could get a notification when a download fails I could go check the logs and deal with that video manually.

Adding an "on_error" option to the "when" (before_dl, pre_process, etc.) param of "--exec" would work.

### Provide verbose output that clearly demonstrates the problem

  * Run **your** yt-dlp command with **-vU** flag added (`yt-dlp -vU <your command line>`)
  * If using API, add `'verbose': True` to `YoutubeDL` params instead
  * Copy the WHOLE output (starting with `[debug] Command-line config`) and insert it below

### Checklist

  * I'm requesting a feature unrelated to a specific site
  * I've looked through the [README](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp#readme)
  * I've verified that I have **updated yt-dlp to nightly or master** ([update instructions](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp#update-channels))
  * I've searched the [bugtracker](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues?q=is%3Aissue%20-label%3Aspam%20%20) for similar requests **including closed ones**. DO NOT post duplicates
  * I've read the [policy against AI/LLM contributions](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#automated-contributions-ai--llm-policy) and understand I may be blocked from the repository if it is violated



### Provide a description that is worded well enough to be understood

Can we get a riscv linux build (only 64-bit is relevant I think) next release?

  * Run **your** yt-dlp command with **-vU** flag added (`yt-dlp -vU <your command line>`)
  * If using API, add `'verbose': True` to `YoutubeDL` params instead
  * Copy the WHOLE output (starting with `[debug] Command-line config`) and insert it below

  * I'm requesting a feature unrelated to a specific site

  * I've verified that I have **updated yt-dlp to nightly or master** ([update instructions](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp#update-channels))
  * I've searched the [bugtracker](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues?q=is%3Aissue%20-label%3Aspam%20%20) for similar requests **including closed ones**. DO NOT post duplicates
  * I've read the [policy against AI/LLM contributions](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#automated-contributions-ai--llm-policy) and understand I may be blocked from the repository if it is violated



### Provide a description that is worded well enough to be understood

I know this isn't me requesting a bug or anything like that but...

I wanna know if you can implement a detection for when you're trying to download a video/audio on a storage that's running out of space and try to warn and cancel the download!

This happens to me on my phone (specifically an unofficial GUI app (YTDLnis)) that when the download is complete, when i check for the file... it doesn't appear there!  
Tried to download using an SD Card (which i know is running out of space)...Checked the logs and it seems fine.

### Provide verbose output that clearly demonstrates the problem

  * Run **your** yt-dlp command with **-vU** flag added (`yt-dlp -vU <your command line>`)
  * If using API, add `'verbose': True` to `YoutubeDL` params instead
  * Copy the WHOLE output (starting with `[debug] Command-line config`) and insert it below

## Description

[](https://github.com/nonopolarity)

[nonopolarity](https://github.com/nonopolarity)

opened [on Mar 19, 2026](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/16279#issue-4100040104)

Issue body actions

### Checklist

  * I'm requesting a feature unrelated to a specific site
  * I've looked through the [README](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp#readme)
  * I've verified that I have **updated yt-dlp to nightly or master** ([update instructions](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp#update-channels))
  * I've searched the [bugtracker](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues?q=is%3Aissue%20-label%3Aspam%20%20) for similar requests **including closed ones**. DO NOT post duplicates
  * I've read the [policy against AI/LLM contributions](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#automated-contributions-ai--llm-policy) and understand I may be blocked from the repository if it is violated



### Provide a description that is worded well enough to be understood

To make it slow down a bit when downloading several videos in a channel, I may use
    
    
    --sleep-interval 180 --max-sleep-interval 300
    

which is to sleep 3 to 5 minutes between each download.

However, **I noticed that it even sleep before the first download, which appears unnecessary.**  
It only needs to be "between" each download. It doesn't need to be "before each download".

### Provide verbose output that clearly demonstrates the problem

  * Run **your** yt-dlp command with **-vU** flag added (`yt-dlp -vU <your command line>`)
  * If using API, add `'verbose': True` to `YoutubeDL` params instead
  * Copy the WHOLE output (starting with `[debug] Command-line config`) and insert it below



### Complete Verbose Output

# Include videos skipped due to download archive in playlist metadata entries #15779

Include videos skipped due to download archive in playlist metadata entries#15779

Copy link

Labels

[enhancementNew feature or request](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues?q=state%3Aopen%20label%3A%22enhancement%22)New feature or request[triageUntriaged issue](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues?q=state%3Aopen%20label%3A%22triage%22)Untriaged issue

[](https://github.com/ctengel)

## Description

[](https://github.com/ctengel)

[ctengel](https://github.com/ctengel)

opened [on Jan 31, 2026](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/15779#issue-3879075038)

Issue body actions

### Checklist

  * I'm requesting a feature unrelated to a specific site
  * I've looked through the [README](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp#readme)
  * I've verified that I have **updated yt-dlp to nightly or master** ([update instructions](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp#update-channels))
  * I've searched the [bugtracker](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues?q=is%3Aissue%20-label%3Aspam%20%20) for similar requests **including closed ones**. DO NOT post duplicates
  * I've read the [policy against AI/LLM contributions](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#automated-contributions-ai--llm-policy) and understand I may be blocked from the repository if it is violated



### Provide a description that is worded well enough to be understood

Desired behavior:

  * User specifies a playlist URL
  * User specifies a download archive file
  * Any video in download archive gets skipped
  * Every video gets at least some basic metadata (extractor, ID, URL) included in output (via `-J` option, playlist `playlist` post-processor, return value `dict`, and/or `.info.json` file



Current behavior:

  * For non-skipped videos, extensive metadata is made available (via `-J`, to `playlist` processor, etc)
  * For skipped videos, no metadata is present whatsoever; `entries` does not have any indication of other videos; only a higher `playlist_count`



Related issues:

  * Current behavior may have been introduced with [-J with --download-archive returns undesirable 4-field-object entries #4369](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/4369) (previously it may have been more similar to "desired behavior"); simply reverting related commit(s) may resolve this issue and enable this use case, but would probably cause others for other use cases. However, it provides some clues how to implement this one.
  * If [Add `--use-postprocessor` WHEN stage `before_playlist` #7034](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/7034) `before_playlist` were to be implemented, it may provide an alternative way to reach a similar goal. (i.e. make entire playlist basic metadata available outside of yt-dlp prior to removing entries from download archive) Suggest evaluating whether this issue or that makes more sense for implementation.



Design alternatives:

  * Include skipped video in `entries` list with dictionary item like `"skipped": True`
  * New config option that instructs yt-dlp to include metadata for skipped videos
  * Add a new list to output (alongside, not in, `entries` list) like `"skipped_entries": [{"ie_key": "extractor", "id": "abcd", "_type": "url", "url": "https://www.extractor.com/abcd"}, {"ie_key": "extractor", "id": "efgh", "_type": "url", "url": "https://www.extractor.com/efgh"}]`



For clarity, abbreviated simulated output illustrating debug output of encountering two videos ("video1" and "video2"), but JSON output excluding "video1" included.

I am willing to work on a pull request for this but looking for feedback on the feature itself and if there is a preference for one design over another.

### Provide verbose output that clearly demonstrates the problem

  * Run **your** yt-dlp command with **-vU** flag added (`yt-dlp -vU <your command line>`)
  * If using API, add `'verbose': True` to `YoutubeDL` params instead
  * Copy the WHOLE output (starting with `[debug] Command-line config`) and insert it below

  * I'm reporting a bug unrelated to a specific site

  * I've searched [known issues](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/3766), [the FAQ](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/wiki/FAQ), and the [bugtracker](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues?q=is%3Aissue%20-label%3Aspam%20%20) for similar issues **including closed ones**. DO NOT post duplicates
  * I've read the [policy against AI/LLM contributions](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#automated-contributions-ai--llm-policy) and understand I may be blocked from the repository if it is violated



### Provide a description that is worded well enough to be understood

If I specify an invalid value for the -f parameter, I get a backtrace:
    
    
    # yt-dlp -vU -f hls-763+ https://www.zdf.de/filme/collection-index-page-ard-collection-ard-dxjuomfyzdpzag93ojg3mgrinzhlyjbhyje5nzk-108
      [... shortened, see "verbose output" section for complete output ...]
      File "/usr/lib/python3.13/site-packages/yt_dlp/YoutubeDL.py", line 2407, in _parse_format_selection
        raise syntax_error('Expected a selector', start)
    SyntaxError: Invalid format specification: Expected a selector
            hls-763+
    

Of course, `-f hls-763+` is obviously invalid since it misses the selected audio stream after the `+` (copy&paste error done by me) so it's correct that yt-dlp errors out.

However, I'd hope for a _more user-friendly error message_ instead of a backtrace. For example, yt-dlp could print something like `Error: value given for -f parameter is invalid.`

### Provide verbose output that clearly demonstrates the problem

  * Run **your** yt-dlp command with **-vU** flag added (`yt-dlp -vU <your command line>`)
  * If using API, add `'verbose': True` to `YoutubeDL` params instead
  * Copy the WHOLE output (starting with `[debug] Command-line config`) and insert it below

## Description

Issue body actions

### Checklist

  * I'm requesting a feature unrelated to a specific site
  * I've looked through the [README](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp#readme)

  * I've searched the [bugtracker](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues?q=is%3Aissue%20-label%3Aspam%20%20) for similar requests **including closed ones**. DO NOT post duplicates
  * I've read the [policy against AI/LLM contributions](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#automated-contributions-ai--llm-policy) and understand I may be blocked from the repository if it is violated



### Provide a description that is worded well enough to be understood

Hello, thank you so much for adding the "aria2c" feature, which is useful if the download speed is throttled ! 💯 🥇

However, it seems that "Surge" is faster than "aria2c" according to the benchmark tests conducted by the Surge Team.  
So it would be great please if amazing yt-dlp Team could add support for "Surge" download engine if it's not too technically complicated please. Thanks!

<https://github.com/surge-downloader/surge?tab=readme-ov-file#benchmarks>

Also, i think adding sequential download feature to yt-dlp is vital capital to allowing us to temporarily play TS videos while downloading—ideal when our Wi-Fi connection becomes too weak,

and

what caught my attention in "Surge" download engine is this feature:

"Sequential Download: Option to download files in strict order (Streaming Mode). Ideal for media files that you want to preview while downloading."

I'm not an expert, but if it's not too technically complex, it would be great please that great "yt-dlp" Team to add support for "Surge" as an alternative download engine to take advantage of sequential downloading to enjoy fast sequential download in order to preview/play video while downloading ideal for weak wifi connexion please, thanks!

<https://github.com/surge-downloader/surge>

### Provide verbose output that clearly demonstrates the problem

  * Run **your** yt-dlp command with **-vU** flag added (`yt-dlp -vU <your command line>`)
  * If using API, add `'verbose': True` to `YoutubeDL` params instead
  * Copy the WHOLE output (starting with `[debug] Command-line config`) and insert it below

## Description

[](https://github.com/Suntooth)

[Suntooth](https://github.com/Suntooth)

opened [on Feb 27, 2026](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/16083#issue-4002746770)

Issue body actions

### Checklist

  * I'm reporting that yt-dlp is broken on a **supported** site
  * I've verified that I have **updated yt-dlp to nightly or master** ([update instructions](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp#update-channels))
  * I've checked that all provided URLs are playable in a browser with the same IP and same login details
  * I've checked that all URLs and arguments with special characters are [properly quoted or escaped](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/wiki/FAQ#video-url-contains-an-ampersand--and-im-getting-some-strange-output-1-2839-or-v-is-not-recognized-as-an-internal-or-external-command)
  * I've searched [known issues](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/3766), [the FAQ](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/wiki/FAQ), and the [bugtracker](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues?q=is%3Aissue%20-label%3Aspam%20%20) for similar issues **including closed ones**. DO NOT post duplicates
  * I've read the [policy against AI/LLM contributions](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#automated-contributions-ai--llm-policy) and understand I may be blocked from the repository if it is violated
  * I've read about [sharing account credentials](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#are-you-willing-to-share-account-details-if-needed) and I'm willing to share it if required



### Region

_No response_

### Provide a description that is worded well enough to be understood

When downloading a Youtube video where the thumbnail has previously been downloaded (such as if it's continuing a partial video download), the existence of thumbnail format 41 seems to be checked _before_ checking if there's a thumbnail already on disk. On the videos where thumbnail 41 _does_ exist, I've seen it download it again then overwrite the already-present thumbnail when converted to JPG by `--convert-thumbnails` (off the top of my head I don't immediately know any videos that have thumbnail 41 to show this, though).

### Provide verbose output that clearly demonstrates the problem

  * Run **your** yt-dlp command with **-vU** flag added (`yt-dlp -vU <your command line>`)
  * If using API, add `'verbose': True` to `YoutubeDL` params instead
  * Copy the WHOLE output (starting with `[debug] Command-line config`) and insert it below

## Description

[](https://github.com/Jack-Sibley)

[Jack-Sibley](https://github.com/Jack-Sibley)

opened [on Jan 30, 2026](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/15773#issue-3877673532)

Issue body actions

### Checklist

  * I'm requesting a feature unrelated to a specific site
  * I've looked through the [README](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp#readme)
  * I've verified that I have **updated yt-dlp to nightly or master** ([update instructions](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp#update-channels))
  * I've searched the [bugtracker](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues?q=is%3Aissue%20-label%3Aspam%20%20) for similar requests **including closed ones**. DO NOT post duplicates
  * I've read the [policy against AI/LLM contributions](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#automated-contributions-ai--llm-policy) and understand I may be blocked from the repository if it is violated



### Provide a description that is worded well enough to be understood

JW Player supports chapters via an attached VTT track with a `kind` of `chapters` ([See docs](https://docs.jwplayer.com/players/docs/jw8-add-chapter-markers)). As an example use case, when downloading videos from Beacon, I would like to preserve this information.

From what I can tell, much of the work necessary to implement this is already covered, `_parse_jwplayer_data()` in `yt_dlp/extractor/common.py` already loops through VTT tracks (currently skipping anything that isn't of kind `captions` or `subtitles`) and there's already a VTT parser in `yt_dlp/webvtt.py` that would be sufficient for processing these files.

The only thing I can't figure out on my own is how best to download the contents of the chapters.vtt file (which is given as a url) and pass it into `parse_fragment()`. All the places where VTT tracks are normally downloaded assume they want to be saved directly into a file.

Any suggestions are appreciated.

### Provide verbose output that clearly demonstrates the problem

  * Run **your** yt-dlp command with **-vU** flag added (`yt-dlp -vU <your command line>`)
  * If using API, add `'verbose': True` to `YoutubeDL` params instead
  * Copy the WHOLE output (starting with `[debug] Command-line config`) and insert it below



### Complete Verbose Output

[](https://github.com/chrizilla)

[chrizilla](https://github.com/chrizilla)

opened [on Jun 8, 2023](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/7264#issue-1748810202)

### DO NOT REMOVE OR SKIP THE ISSUE TEMPLATE

  * I understand that I will be **blocked** if I _intentionally_ remove or skip any mandatory* field



### Checklist

  * I'm reporting that yt-dlp is broken on a **supported** site
  * I've verified that I'm running yt-dlp version **2023.03.04** ([update instructions](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp#update)) or later (specify commit)
  * I've checked that all provided URLs are playable in a browser with the same IP and same login details
  * I've checked that all URLs and arguments with special characters are [properly quoted or escaped](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/wiki/FAQ#video-url-contains-an-ampersand--and-im-getting-some-strange-output-1-2839-or-v-is-not-recognized-as-an-internal-or-external-command)
  * I've searched [known issues](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/3766) and the [bugtracker](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues?q=) for similar issues **including closed ones**. DO NOT post duplicates
  * I've read the [guidelines for opening an issue](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#opening-an-issue)
  * I've read about [sharing account credentials](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#are-you-willing-to-share-account-details-if-needed) and I'm willing to share it if required



### Region

Accessible in Germany/Austria/Switzerland. Possibly worldwide.

### Provide a description that is worded well enough to be understood

### steps to reproduce this issue

  1. disable Widevine as [instructed](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/4062#issuecomment-1153474056) to confirm video is not DRM-protected
  2. open [URL](https://www.sat1.at/tv/videos/der-sat-1-bio-check-aldi-rewe-denns-co-ganze-folge) in Firefox
  3. click on video
  4. site redirects to an [authentication page](https://signin.7pass.de)
  5. login _(signup is free and fast as only email/firstname/bday are required, but can share login credentials if needed)_
  6. site redirects back to URL from step 2
  7. video is now playable in Firefox
  8. run `yt-dlp --no-config -f- -v --cookies-from-browser firefox "URL"`



### expected result

yt-dlp download should start

### actual result

`ERROR: [prosiebensat1] tv/videos/der-sat-1-bio-check-aldi-rewe-denns-co-ganze-folge: Unable to extract clip id; please report this issue on https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues?q= , filling out the appropriate issue template. `

### DO NOT REMOVE OR SKIP THE ISSUE TEMPLATE

  * I understand that I will be **blocked** if I _intentionally_ remove or skip any mandatory* field



### Checklist

  * I'm reporting a new site support request
  * I've verified that I'm running yt-dlp version **2023.03.04** ([update instructions](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp#update)) or later (specify commit)
  * I've checked that all provided URLs are playable in a browser with the same IP and same login details
  * I've checked that none of provided URLs [violate any copyrights](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#is-the-website-primarily-used-for-piracy) or contain any [DRM](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Digital_rights_management) to the best of my knowledge
  * I've searched [known issues](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/3766) and the [bugtracker](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues?q=) for similar issues **including closed ones**. DO NOT post duplicates
  * I've read the [guidelines for opening an issue](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#opening-an-issue)
  * I've read about [sharing account credentials](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#are-you-willing-to-share-account-details-if-needed) and am willing to share it if required



### Region

worldwide

### Example URLs

<https://www.planet-wissen.de/video-lebensglueck--was-uns-zufrieden-macht-100.html>  
<https://www.planet-wissen.de/video-hochwassergefahr--wie-gut-sind-wir-vorbereitet-100.html>

<https://www.planet-wissen.de/video-von-geistergold-und-kristallen--die-faszination-der-mineralien-100.html>

### Provide a description that is worded well enough to be understood

_"Planet Wissen"_ is a German-language information program on all sorts of interesting general education topics.

Sometimes there is another source for the video on one of the TV channels which has broadcasted the specific program.  
For example: This [planet-wissen URL](https://www.planet-wissen.de/video-lebensglueck--was-uns-zufrieden-macht-100.html) is also available [here on this TV channel](https://www.ardmediathek.de/video/Y3JpZDovL3dkci5kZS9CZWl0cmFnLTQwNGZkMjVkLTRhM2QtNDk2MS05MWVkLTlmYTRiZTUzYWFhYQ) which is handled by the `[ARDBetaMediathek]` IE. Maybe this IE could also handle the `planet-wissen.de` URLs ?  
(I don't know, if it's always this TV channel though, or if the program runs on multiple TV channels.)

### Provide verbose output that clearly demonstrates the problem

  * Run **your** yt-dlp command with **-vU** flag added (`yt-dlp -vU <your command line>`)
  * If using API, add `'verbose': True` to `YoutubeDL` params instead
  * Copy the WHOLE output (starting with `[debug] Command-line config`) and insert it below

[orf:tvthek] nested playlists: detect 1st-level playlists#7065

Labels

[site-enhancementFeature request for some website](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues?q=state%3Aopen%20label%3A%22site-enhancement%22)Feature request for some website[triageUntriaged issue](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues?q=state%3Aopen%20label%3A%22triage%22)Untriaged issue

[](https://github.com/chrizilla)

## Description

[](https://github.com/chrizilla)

[chrizilla](https://github.com/chrizilla)

opened [on May 17, 2023](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/7065#issue-1714573828)

Issue body actions

### DO NOT REMOVE OR SKIP THE ISSUE TEMPLATE

  * I understand that I will be **blocked** if I _intentionally_ remove or skip any mandatory* field



### Checklist

  * I'm requesting a site-specific feature
  * I've verified that I'm running yt-dlp version **2023.03.04** ([update instructions](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp#update)) or later (specify commit)
  * I've checked that all provided URLs are playable in a browser with the same IP and same login details
  * I've searched [known issues](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/3766) and the [bugtracker](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues?q=) for similar issues **including closed ones**. DO NOT post duplicates
  * I've read the [guidelines for opening an issue](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#opening-an-issue)
  * I've read about [sharing account credentials](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#are-you-willing-to-share-account-details-if-needed) and I'm willing to share it if required



### Region

Austria:yes, worldwide:maybe

### Example URLs

Example URLs are cited below, but almost all URLs expire within 7 days after broadcast so new URLs might be required.

### Provide a description that is worded well enough to be understood

## basic information

URLs from [orf:tvthek] mostly follow this pattern:

`https://tvthek.orf.at/profile/[broadcast_series]/[broadcast_series_ID]/[broadcast_episode]/[broadcast_episode_ID]`  
example:  
<https://tvthek.orf.at/profile/Themenmontag/13687392/Themenmontag-Die-Wahrheit-ueber-Fisch/14179024>

## problem

But [orf:tvthek] extractor doesn't yet interpret the URL as a playlist if only the playlist URL is given.  
Example:  
<https://tvthek.orf.at/profile/Themenmontag/13687392>  
i.e. `https://tvthek.orf.at/profile/[broadcast_series]/[broadcast_series_ID]`  
... is not recognized as a playlist.

## suggested solution

**Basically there are two different URLs listing the playlist entries:**

  * <https://tvthek.orf.at/profile/Themenmontag/13687392/>  
The playlist entries are listed below under the linkified header _"Weitere Ausgaben dieser Sendung"_ (german for _"more episodes of this broadcast"_), which links to the URL below ("......./episodes")
  * <https://tvthek.orf.at/profile/Themenmontag/13687392/episodes>



It would be helpful if the extractor could recognize **both** of these URLs as playlists.

### Provide verbose output that clearly demonstrates the problem

  * Run **your** yt-dlp command with **-vU** flag added (`yt-dlp -vU <your command line>`)
  * If using API, add `'verbose': True` to `YoutubeDL` params instead
  * Copy the WHOLE output (starting with `[debug] Command-line config`) and insert it below



### Complete Verbose Output

### Provide a description that is worded well enough to be understood

    Sleeping 4096.00 seconds ...
    

I don't think this makes much sense.

If an error occurs (such as above), `--retry-sleep` sends yt-dlp to sleep, ok.  
Now, when yt-dlp wakes up from sleep and

  * ... immediately fails again, yt-dlp should be sent back to sleep and the sleep time be augmented exponentially (which is currently done)
  * ... does not immediately fail again (i.e. successfully continues to download), the **sleep time counter should be reset**.



## rationale

IMO the reason for exponential sleep time is to avoid continuously bumping into the same error with linear sleep time (i.e. trying to download every 2 seconds does not help when the server is currently down). Exponential sleep time is there sleep longer and longer and longer ... until the error goes away. But when the error has gone away, the counter should be reset, because it otherwise hampers the download unnecessarily (as shown in the example above).

### Provide verbose output that clearly demonstrates the problem

  * Run **your** yt-dlp command with **-vU** flag added (`yt-dlp -vU <your command line>`)
  * If using API, add `'verbose': True` to `YoutubeDL` params instead
  * Copy the WHOLE output (starting with `[debug] Command-line config`) and insert it below

## Description

[](https://github.com/chrizilla)

[chrizilla](https://github.com/chrizilla)

opened [on May 2, 2023](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/6974#issue-1692960443)

### DO NOT REMOVE OR SKIP THE ISSUE TEMPLATE

  * I understand that I will be **blocked** if I _intentionally_ remove or skip any mandatory* field



### Checklist

  * I'm requesting a feature unrelated to a specific site
  * I've looked through the [README](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp#readme)
  * I've verified that I'm running yt-dlp version **2023.03.04** ([update instructions](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp#update)) or later (specify commit)
  * I've searched [known issues](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/3766) and the [bugtracker](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues?q=) for similar issues **including closed ones**. DO NOT post duplicates
  * I've read the [guidelines for opening an issue](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#opening-an-issue)



### Provide a description that is worded well enough to be understood

# problem

When a `-o` filepath\filename template consists of multiple fields, and the sum of the length of all these fields must not exceed  
`OS limit - (length of the temporary files appendix + length of yt-dlp download base path)`, the problem is how to best curtail these fields, which can vary considerably in length and are therefore unpredictable.

To simplify:  
It's difficult to ensure `A+B+C+D < OS limit` when `A`, `B`, `C`, `D` greatly vary in length.

While it is certainly possible to set a dumb limit for each field: `A.50+B.50+C.50+D.50 + base path + appendix < 255`  
this is not a intelligent solution, if for example
    
    
    A = 120 bytes
    B = 50 bytes
    C = 10 bytes
    D = 20 bytes
    

because in this case `A` will be unnecessarily truncated to less than half its length.

# example

`-o "%(alt_title,title).100B\%(title).100B [%(extractor)s.%(id)s] {%(format_id)s}.%(ext)s"`

  * `extractor` is quite short and doesn't require any further shortening
  * cutting off `id` and `format_id` makes them useless, although they can become quite lengthy in some cases
  * so that leaves us only with `alt_title` and `title` which can be shortened



The above template should work in most cases, but can still exceed the OS limit when `id` and/or `format_id` are lengthy.

# current solutions

  1. So one solution would be to add further curtailing:  
`-o "%(alt_title,title).40B\%(title).100B [%(extractor)s.%(id)s] {%(format_id)s}.%(ext)s"`  
But this shortens the video directory so severely that it becomes barely readable.

  2. `--trim-filenames` but [Behavior of --trim-filenames is not clear #3494](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/3494) and possibly broken:

> This should produce the file `../testfolder/Me at.webm`, but instead it produces the file `testf.webm`.
> 
> Worse still, if the `--output` argument is an absolute path like `/home/myname/folder/folder/stuff`, yt-dlp will try to create a file in the root directory called `/home/.webm`.
> 
> So, I think `--trim-filenames` is broken.

and from [“--trim-filenames” failure！pls check it. #5499 (comment)](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/5499#issuecomment-1311939459) :

> the whole path will be trimmed, not only the filename. The file might end up in one of the parent directories.

so this is [not a recommended solution](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/3494#issuecomment-1103969834) :

> I honestly recommend using something like [outtmpl] instead to control the filename length

and [\--trim-filenames fails to clip file name properly when there is a dot in a video title #2314 (comment)](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/2314#issuecomment-1011295071) :

> I am aware of this issue 😓. The `--trim-filename` option is just overall poorly implemented, making this tricky to fix. I honestly suggest using something like `%(title).30B.%(ext)s` instead

and [here](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/1837#issuecomment-981907118):

> `--trim-filename` was added in youtube-dlc and actually quite buggy. I can fix this particular issue, but I recommend using the string formatting to achieve a similar effect. Eg: `-o %(title).200s.%(ext)s`




# enhancement idea

It would really be great to be able to intelligently trim the filename, i.e. trim

  1. **ONLY in case it is needed ...**  
(The idea is a bit like in [\--restrict-filenames only as fallback #6972](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/6972) to use this enhancement **"only as a fallback"** in case it is needed.)

  2. **... and at a user-defined place.**  
(As opposed to `--trim-filenames` which trims at end, thereby causing the same errors in my tests as described by [@axcore](https://github.com/axcore) above in [Behavior of --trim-filenames is not clear #3494](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/3494) and [@Fabian42](https://github.com/Fabian42) in [String length limit #1888](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/1888):




> What currently happens if I use `--trim-filenames` is that the ID gets cut off completely if the title is too long. In the worst case, if I'm downloading a playlist of videos with titles like "Super long series title, episode 42: XYZ", I would get completely identical filenames and all downloads after the first one would get skipped.

# implemenation

The user can indicate at which position this intelligent trim should occur if needed.  
Something like:

  * `-o "%(alt_title,title).100B+\%(title).100B [%(extractor)s.%(id)s] {%(format_id)s}.%(ext)s"` : the plus sign indicates that this field can be trimmed **further** than the 100B if otherwise the entire path\filename length exceeded OS limits.
  * `-o "%(alt_title,title){100B-excesslength}\%(title).100B [%(extractor)s.%(id)s] {%(format_id)s}.%(ext)s"`



Maybe you'll find better implementation ideas.

It would also be a good idea to come up with some solution that would kick in by default (so that all users benefit from this enhancement and not just the 1% who dig into the jungle of parameters).

# benefits

  * If the filepath becomes too long, this enhancement would save the download from failing.
  * On the other hand, the filename length allowed by the OS can be fully used with this enhancement (as opposed to the currently possible solutions, where a "safe" filename template like `-o "%(alt_title,title).40B\%(title).40B [%(extractor)s.%(id)s] {%(format_id)s}.%(ext)s"` would waste / give away a lot of available space.
  * This would allow trimming long paths at a user-defined position where it hurts less than at the end with `--trim-filenames`.



# workaround

What I currently do is essentially going back and forth between different config files:

  * I have very generous length limits but therefore often run into filename-too-long problem.
  * I then manually increase the length limit ristriction in my config file,
  * delete the leftover files from the 1st run,
  * run yt-dlp again and ...
  * most of the time forget to reset the config file to its previous state,
  * so that the filenames of my subsequent downloads are also truncated. 🙁



# related

  * [[Feature request] Handle Long filenames in default template and temporary files #1136](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/1136)
  * [Behavior of --trim-filenames is not clear #3494](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/3494)
  * [\--trim-filenames fails to clip file name properly when there is a dot in a video title #2314](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/2314)

  * If using API, add `'verbose': True` to `YoutubeDL` params instead
  * Copy the WHOLE output (starting with `[debug] Command-line config`) and insert it below

opened [on May 3, 2023](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/6983#issue-1694998244)

Issue body actions

### DO NOT REMOVE OR SKIP THE ISSUE TEMPLATE

  * I understand that I will be **blocked** if I _intentionally_ remove or skip any mandatory* field



### Checklist

  * I'm requesting a feature unrelated to a specific site
  * I've looked through the [README](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp#readme)
  * I've verified that I'm running yt-dlp version **2023.03.04** ([update instructions](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp#update)) or later (specify commit)
  * I've searched [known issues](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/3766) and the [bugtracker](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues?q=) for similar issues **including closed ones**. DO NOT post duplicates
  * I've read the [guidelines for opening an issue](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#opening-an-issue)



### Provide a description that is worded well enough to be understood

(Asking here so as not to lead [#1136](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/1136) further off-topic.)

In [#1136 (comment)](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/1136#issuecomment-1503888641) a solution was proposed to mark truncated filenames in `-o` template:

> Add a `%(title.201&…|)s` \- read as "if `title.201` (201'th char) exists, then (`&`) add `…`, else (`|`) add nothing"

This works for character count but apparently not for the subsequently discussed byte count (which may be more useful when dealing with unicode chars):
    
    
    yt-dlp ZYlALC1Pmv4 --skip-download --no-config --print "%(title).50s%(title.51&…|)s"
    Hubble Space Telescope, Planet 9, Curiosity Mars R…    # truncates at 50 chars and detects 51st char
    
    yt-dlp ZYlALC1Pmv4 --skip-download --no-config --print "%(title).50B%(title.51B&…|)s"
    Hubble Space Telescope, Planet 9, Curiosity Mars R     # truncates at 50 bytes but doesn't detect 51st byte

I guess this is either the wrong syntax or not yet possible to do.  
In the latter case, would it be worth considering this new syntax as an enhancement ?

### Provide verbose output that clearly demonstrates the problem

  * Run **your** yt-dlp command with **-vU** flag added (`yt-dlp -vU <your command line>`)
  * If using API, add `'verbose': True` to `YoutubeDL` params instead
  * Copy the WHOLE output (starting with `[debug] Command-line config`) and insert it below



### Complete Verbose Output

_No response_

# IF operator for boolean fields #6851

## Description

[](https://github.com/chrizilla)

[chrizilla](https://github.com/chrizilla)

opened [on Apr 18, 2023](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/6851#issue-1672396347)

Issue body actions

### DO NOT REMOVE OR SKIP THE ISSUE TEMPLATE

  * I understand that I will be **blocked** if I _intentionally_ remove or skip any mandatory* field



### Checklist

  * I'm requesting a feature unrelated to a specific site
  * I've looked through the [README](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp#readme)
  * I've verified that I'm running yt-dlp version **2023.03.04** ([update instructions](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp#update)) or later (specify commit)
  * I've searched [known issues](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/3766) and the [bugtracker](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues?q=) for similar issues **including closed ones**. DO NOT post duplicates
  * I've read the [guidelines for opening an issue](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#opening-an-issue)



### Provide a description that is worded well enough to be understood

I don't know if it's difficult to implement, but just to put the idea out there:

# feature suggestion

It would be helpful if boolean field values (true/false) could be tested with an IF operator (either the current `&` operator or a new one).

# example
    
    
    yt-dlp TSNbCSF13Zo --skip-download --no-config --print is_live
    False
    
    yt-dlp TSNbCSF13Zo --skip-download --no-config --print "%(is_live&live|notlive)s"
    live    # should be "notlive" because is_live=false

# implementation

  * either change the existing behaviour so that for boolean variables not the existence is checked but its true/false value, so that `boolean_variable_with_value_false&` = `false` (and not `true` as currently handled)
  * or [a new operator is required](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/6848#issuecomment-1512427900) for this
  * or it could also be solved by allowing logical operations in the `________&` part, for example: 
    * `%(is_live=true&live|notlive)s`
    * `%(duration<1800&short film|)s`



# use cases

  * [safety measure: add epoch to `-o` if `is_live=true` OR generic filename #6852](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/6852)
  * [[Feature Request] Output Template: support for new fields (height, width, chosen_format_id) and/or support for IF comparisons/qualifiers #6300](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/6300)
  * [add "live" string to filename template if `is_live=true` ? #6848](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/6848)



### Provide verbose output that clearly demonstrates the problem

  * Run **your** yt-dlp command with **-vU** flag added (`yt-dlp -vU <your command line>`)
  * If using API, add `'verbose': True` to `YoutubeDL` params instead
  * Copy the WHOLE output (starting with `[debug] Command-line config`) and insert it below

### Checklist

  * I'm reporting a new site support request
  * I've verified that I have **updated yt-dlp to nightly or master** ([update instructions](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp#update-channels))
  * I've checked that all provided URLs are playable in a browser with the same IP and same login details
  * I've checked that none of provided URLs [violate any copyrights](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#is-the-website-primarily-used-for-piracy) or contain any [DRM](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Digital_rights_management) to the best of my knowledge
  * I've searched the [bugtracker](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues?q=is%3Aissue%20-label%3Aspam%20%20) for similar requests **including closed ones**. DO NOT post duplicates
  * I've read the [policy against AI/LLM contributions](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#automated-contributions-ai--llm-policy) and understand I may be blocked from the repository if it is violated
  * I've read about [sharing account credentials](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#are-you-willing-to-share-account-details-if-needed) and am willing to share it if required



### Region

Germany

### Example URLs

Live 24/7 Free - <https://myaew.com/video/b8441e5b-b1e4-4d7b-af95-a04312cabc87/QUVXX0ZSRUU=>

### Provide a description that is worded well enough to be understood

This 24/7 live stream requires a free account to access the video. The video itself is not protected by DRM.

### Provide verbose output that clearly demonstrates the problem

  * Run **your** yt-dlp command with **-vU** flag added (`yt-dlp -vU <your command line>`)
  * If using API, add `'verbose': True` to `YoutubeDL` params instead
  * Copy the WHOLE output (starting with `[debug] Command-line config`) and insert it below

Issue body actions

### Checklist

  * I'm reporting a new site support request
  * I've verified that I have **updated yt-dlp to nightly or master** ([update instructions](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp#update-channels))
  * I've checked that all provided URLs are playable in a browser with the same IP and same login details
  * I've checked that none of provided URLs [violate any copyrights](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#is-the-website-primarily-used-for-piracy) or contain any [DRM](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Digital_rights_management) to the best of my knowledge
  * I've searched the [bugtracker](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues?q=is%3Aissue%20-label%3Aspam%20%20) for similar requests **including closed ones**. DO NOT post duplicates
  * I've read the [policy against AI/LLM contributions](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#automated-contributions-ai--llm-policy) and understand I may be blocked from the repository if it is violated
  * I've read about [sharing account credentials](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#are-you-willing-to-share-account-details-if-needed) and am willing to share it if required



### Region

India

### Example URLs

  * Single video: <https://sainaplay.com/movie/pookkalam-varavayi/gf7a9ad8j8tt>



### Provide a description that is worded well enough to be understood

SainaPlay is an Indian OTT platform that streams Malayalam movies.

Currently yt-dlp does not support downloading videos from this site.  
Please add extractor support for SainaPlay.

Example URL:  
<https://sainaplay.com/movie/pookkalam-varavayi/gf7a9ad8j8tt>

The site requires a user account to watch videos.  
Some newer movies require an active subscription, while older movies can be watched without a subscription after logging in.

Region: India.

### Provide verbose output that clearly demonstrates the problem

  * Run **your** yt-dlp command with **-vU** flag added (`yt-dlp -vU <your command line>`)
  * If using API, add `'verbose': True` to `YoutubeDL` params instead
  * Copy the WHOLE output (starting with `[debug] Command-line config`) and insert it below

### Checklist

  * I'm reporting a new site support request
  * I've verified that I have **updated yt-dlp to nightly or master** ([update instructions](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp#update-channels))
  * I've checked that all provided URLs are playable in a browser with the same IP and same login details
  * I've checked that none of provided URLs [violate any copyrights](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#is-the-website-primarily-used-for-piracy) or contain any [DRM](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Digital_rights_management) to the best of my knowledge
  * I've searched the [bugtracker](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues?q=is%3Aissue%20-label%3Aspam%20%20) for similar requests **including closed ones**. DO NOT post duplicates
  * I've read the [policy against AI/LLM contributions](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#automated-contributions-ai--llm-policy) and understand I may be blocked from the repository if it is violated
  * I've read about [sharing account credentials](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#are-you-willing-to-share-account-details-if-needed) and am willing to share it if required

  * I've checked that all URLs and arguments with special characters are [properly quoted or escaped](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/wiki/FAQ#video-url-contains-an-ampersand--and-im-getting-some-strange-output-1-2839-or-v-is-not-recognized-as-an-internal-or-external-command)
  * I've searched [known issues](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/3766), [the FAQ](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/wiki/FAQ), and the [bugtracker](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues?q=is%3Aissue%20-label%3Aspam%20%20) for similar issues **including closed ones**. DO NOT post duplicates
  * I've read the [policy against AI/LLM contributions](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#automated-contributions-ai--llm-policy) and understand I may be blocked from the repository if it is violated
  * I've read about [sharing account credentials](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#are-you-willing-to-share-account-details-if-needed) and I'm willing to share it if required

I got the manifest url: <https://vod3.cf.dmcdn.net/sec2(unc5TXvUavOqHxB0eWV2vH57JIks2kiLBzA7DUR7cAXsvnqZXt9nNl-f-AgYpeqaaPTmjhW_pfi3buNfJe7SV6rpT0pnnv8Gu-9lVI1uEQb9ghtSVlkcth_aJSTq35o2p-gs8LXWg3852PgCa6VyQtSV7kPt4VM-vgk6C_Gkd6O810NdlQ-lcp8NNQo8NUoAgC3rV2q6oYMtvucvzslSWw)/video/fmp4/610231850/h264_aac_hd/2/manifest.m3u8#cell=cf3>

When I add it to yt-dlp it only downloads a small file, doesn't actually catch the manifest streams and begins download. Not sure why this is happening. Tried it on N_m3u8DL-RE and it works, the video does not have DRM, its a simple Fmp4. Only gives a file of about 30k and not a 1gb video file. I have attached the file for reference:

manifest.manifest.mp4

  * I've checked that none of provided URLs [violate any copyrights](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#is-the-website-primarily-used-for-piracy) or contain any [DRM](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Digital_rights_management) to the best of my knowledge
  * I've searched the [bugtracker](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues?q=is%3Aissue%20-label%3Aspam%20%20) for similar requests **including closed ones**. DO NOT post duplicates
  * I've read the [policy against AI/LLM contributions](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#automated-contributions-ai--llm-policy) and understand I may be blocked from the repository if it is violated
  * I've read about [sharing account credentials](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#are-you-willing-to-share-account-details-if-needed) and am willing to share it if required



### Region

Anywhere

### Example URLs

<https://blacksky.community/profile/did:plc:tpv66pk3fqlpfudmh5zi3hzo/post/3mgjxbnwktk26>

### Provide a description that is worded well enough to be understood

Blacksky has recently diverged from the featureset of bluesky to the point where it now supports 60fps video where bluesky does not, so proper support for blacksky.community URLs are appreciated  
fwiw this is currently worked around by just using the bsky.app URL. Bluesky proper will not play these out-of-spec videos but will happily hand over the blob URL over to yt-dlp

### Provide verbose output that clearly demonstrates the problem

  * Run **your** yt-dlp command with **-vU** flag added (`yt-dlp -vU <your command line>`)
  * If using API, add `'verbose': True` to `YoutubeDL` params instead
  * Copy the WHOLE output (starting with `[debug] Command-line config`) and insert it below

### Description of your _pull request_ and other information

Not sure what to call this.

This code was originally from [#682](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/pull/682).

This PR adds:

  * fallback player url extraction when it fails to be extracted from the webpage
  * don't download js player unnecessarily for clients that don't require it
  * try extract js player url from any additional client configs
  * ability to skip the js player usage/download (inc iframe fallback). 
    * This overrides the clients' config setting.
    * **This can be enabled with`--extractor-args youtube:player_skip=js`**
    * Formats that require signature decryption will be skipped automatically (since no player url)
  * ability to skip the webpage download 
    * **This can be enabled with`--extractor-args youtube:player_skip=webpage`**



KNOWN ISSUES:

  * authentication for multi-channel accounts and multi-account cookies may not work correctly if the webpage (and any additional client configs) are not downloaded.



TODO:

  * documentation
  * `player_skip=js` or something else?

Some example usage

  1. `--extractor-args youtube:player_skip=webpage,configs,js;player_client=android,web`
     * This makes extraction solely rely on the API - so no webpage downloads. Might help with avoiding 429s in some situations.
     * Since the web client usually needs the player js, formats from the web client requiring signature decryption will be skipped.
     * 3 initial API requests (android, web, initial data)

~~2.`--extractor-args youtube:player_skip=webpage,configs,js;player_client=android`  
\- Same as above, but without the web client (some minor metadata may be missed - be sure to check)  
\- 2 initial API requests (android, initial data)~~ **Do not use - missing metadata** ~~3.`--extractor-args youtube:player_skip=webpage;player_client=android`  
\- since the android client doesn't require the player js, this is the same as 2.~~ **Do not use - missing metadata**

  4. `--extractor-args youtube:player_skip=webpage`
     * basically forces fallbacks as if the webpage failed to download.
     * player url should be downloaded using the iframe API fallback (once, only if required)
  5. `--extractor-args youtube:player_skip=webpage;player_client=web_music`
     * config webpage for web_music is downloaded (thus player js details), so web formats should work correctly.

Not recommended:

  1. `--extractor-args youtube:player_skip=webpage,configs,js;player_client=web`
     * In some cases you'll get a no formats error (formats from the web client requiring signature decryption will be skipped).
  2. `--extractor-args youtube:player_skip=js;player_client=web`
